We invoke you with oblations at evening and at dawn, like hunters seeking wild elephants.
You, O lords of splendor, bring nourishment to the people who offer the sacrifice according to the seasons.
O Aśvins, Ghoṣā, the daughter of the king, as she was going along, spoke to you both: "O heroes, I ask you:
be present for me by day and be present for me by night; be able to help the one who possesses horses and chariots, and the racing steed.
O Aśvins, you two are sages; like Kutsa, you bring the chariot to the people, and you reach it like a singer.
O Aśvins, the bee brought honey for you both from afar, like a maiden to her appointed tryst.
O Aśvins, you indeed rescued Bhujyu, you rescued Vaśa, and you rescued Śiñjāra who desired [you].
The liberal giver sits around your friendship; through your protection, I have sought your favor.

O Aśvins, you indeed protected Kr̥śa; you protected Śayu; you protected the worshipper and the widow. O Aśvins, for the sake of those seeking gain, you opened the thundering stall that had seven mouths.
The maiden was born; the young man flew forth; the plants grew up according to their wondrous powers.
For him the rivers flow like torrents down a slope; for him this day brings the state of lordship.
They weep for the living and disperse at the sacrifice; the men have fixed their thoughts upon a long-lasting bond.
To the fathers who have prepared this [offering], they bring what is desirable; to the lords of joy, the women come to embrace them.
We do not know that; speak it forth clearly: how is it that the youth dwells within the wombs of the young maidens?

We would go to the home of the beloved bull, the seed-sower of the cow—O Aśvins, that is what we desire. O Lords of ample wealth, may your favor come to us; O Aśvins, desires have been placed within our hearts.
Become our guardians, O divine pair, Lords of Splendor; may we reach the dear dwellings of Aryaman.

Rejoicing in the house of man, bestow upon the eloquent singer wealth accompanied by heroic sons. O Lords of Splendor, provide a ford with good drinking water; strike down the obstacle standing in the path and destroy evil intent.

Where indeed today, in which people’s dwellings, do the Aśvins, the wonder-workers and lords of splendor, rejoice? Who has detained them? To whose house have they gone—that of a sage or of one performing a sacrifice? That same chariot of theirs, invoked by many, worthy of praise, three-wheeled, and ever-coming to the libations— RV_10.040.14.1 {20} Where indeed today, in which people’s dwellings, do the Aśvins, the wonder-workers and lords of splendor, rejoice?
RV_10.040.14.2 {20} Who has detained them? To whose house have they gone—that of a sage or of one performing a sacrifice?
RV_10.41.01.1 {21} That same chariot of theirs, invoked by many, worthy of praise, three-wheeled, and ever-coming to the libations—
With well-fashioned hymns, we invoke at the dawning of the Uṣas the one who wanders around, worthy of the assembly.
O Nāsatyas, you mount at dawn the chariot that is yoked in the morning, which travels early and carries honey.
O Heroes, Aśvins, by means of this chariot you go to the clans that offer sacrifice, even to the sacrifice of the poor man where the Hotṛ priest is present.
Whether you go to the *adhvaryu* with honeyed hands and skillful fingers, or to the *agnīdh* of firm resolve who dwells in the house,
or to the libations of the inspired singer— come from there, O Aśvins, to drink the honeyed draught.
Like an archer shooting his arrow straight forward, and like one preparing for battle, bring forth a hymn of praise for him.

O wise ones, cross over speech with your voice; O singer, cause the noble one to rest—the Soma [juice] for Indra. With milking, win over the cow as a friend; O singer, awaken the lover, Indra. Like a full vessel overflowing with wealth, bring forth the hero for the bestowing of bounty.
RV 10.42.3: Why indeed, O Maghavan, do they call you a liberal giver? Sharpen me; I hear that you are the one who sharpens.
O Śakra, let my inspired thought be effective; O Indra, bring us fortune that finds wealth. RV 10.42.4:
Men, standing together in the heat of battle, invoke you, O Indra, in their desire for possessions.
There, the hero makes him his ally who brings the oblation; he desires no friendship with one who presses no Soma.

To him who for him presses abundant, flowing Soma, offering strong libations and providing nourishment— for him he drives away the swift-moving enemies at dawn, and he slays Vṛtra, making them powerless.

In whomsoever we place our hope, in Indra; he who, as Maghavan, has directed his desire toward us—let his enemy, even though far away, tremble before him; let the human powers bow down before his glory.
Drive the enemy far away with that fierce bolt, O you who are invoked by many!
Bestow upon us wealth consisting of barley and cattle, O Indra; grant the singer a prayer that brings the prize of victory.

Into whom the strong-pressing, sharp Somas have flowed in abundance, reaching their full measure—Indra, the Maghavan, does not fail to bestow his gift; he brings much desirable wealth to the one who presses the juice.
Moreover, he wins by casting the decisive die; the gambler gathers his winnings at the right time. He who desires the gods does not withhold wealth; the self-reliant one pours riches upon him.
O Much-invoked One, may we overcome all ill-fortune with cattle, and hunger with barley.
May we, together with the kings, as the first, win riches through our own vigorous host.

May Bṛhaspati protect us from behind, and from above, and from below, against the one who seeks to harm us. May Indra, our friend, from the front and from the middle, grant wide space to us, his friends.
Toward Indra my thoughts have cried out, seeking the light of heaven, all united and longing for him;
they embrace him as wives embrace a husband, as people embrace a handsome youth, for his protection, the bounteous Maghavan.
My mind does not indeed go elsewhere than toward you; O Much-invoked One, I have fixed my desire solely upon you.

Like a king, O wondrous one, sit down upon the sacrificial grass; let there be a place for you to drink at this excellent Soma. Indra overcomes both want and hunger; he, the bounteous lord, rules over wealth and food. These seven rivers flow down his slope, increasing the vital strength of that impetuous bull.
Like birds upon a tree with fair foliage, the exhilarating Soma drops have settled in Indra’s vessels.
Flashing forth with power like the vanguard of an army, he found the light of heaven for Manu, the Arya.
As a gambler gathers his winnings at play, the Bounteous One won the sun, the prize to be seized.
No other, neither one of old nor one of recent times, O Maghavan, can equal that heroic power of yours.
Maghavan has taken his place around every tribe; the Bull gazes upon the lowing of the people.
He at whose libations Śakra rejoices indeed overcomes his assailants with true and potent Soma-draughts.
When the Soma juices flow together toward Indra like waters toward the ocean, or like rivulets toward a lake;
when the inspired singers increase his greatness at the place of sacrifice, as the rain from heaven increases the barley with its divine bounty.
Like a furious bull he rushes through the mid-air, he who made these waters have the noble man as their lord.
That Maghavan has found light for the man who presses the juice, who gives quickly, and who offers oblations.
May the axe rise up together with light; may it become like the well-yielding cow of the eternal Order (Ṛta).
May the ruddy one shine forth with his brilliance, pure and bright; may the Lord of the Truth blaze with white radiance like the sun.
RV 10.43.10.1: May we cross over this lack of understanding with the help of cows...
RV 10.43.11.1: May Bṛhaspati protect us from all sides...
RV 10.44.1.1: May Indra, the self-ruling lord, come for exhilaration—he who, impetuous by his nature, is exceedingly mighty.

Exerting himself beyond all powers of endurance with his boundless and great virility—your chariot has firm poles and your two bay steeds are well-governed; the thunderbolt, O lord of men, is fixed in your hand.
Come hither quickly, O King, by fair paths; let the bull-like powers of him who has drunk [the Soma] increase.
May those who carry Indra, the fierce ones with fierce mouths and great strength, bring him hither— the king with the thunderbolt in his arm,
the swift, the bull, whose vigor is true— to our feast. Thus you, the bull, seek for yourself the lord who dwells in the wooden vat, the conscious one, the pillar of strength, the supporter.
Exert your power; gather it within you, so that the waters may come for our increase, like those who draw from wells.
May riches come to us, for I have praised you; come to the one who offers Soma, bringing blessings for yourself.
You are the lord; sit upon this sacred grass (barhis). By your law, your vessels are inviolable.
The first invocations of the gods went forth separately; they performed deeds seeking glory that were difficult to surpass.

Those who were unable to board the sacrificial ship, the weaklings, settled down in this world. Thus indeed, let the others, the evil-minded, be far away—those whose ill-yoked horses have been harnessed.
Thus indeed are those who were formerly present for the giving of many provisions and means of enjoyment.
He supported the mountains and the plains as they shook; Heaven thundered and agitated the intermediate regions.
Having drunk from the two joined vessels, he stands firm; intoxicated by the draught, he proclaims the hymns of praise.
I carry this well-fashioned goad for you, O Maghavan, with which you shall break the hoof-breakers.
May there be a hymn of praise for you at this libation; O Maghavan, be present at the pressed juice and the sacrifice, like one who bestows fortune.
With cattle, may we overcome this mental distress...
May Bṛhaspati protect us from all sides...
Agni was first born from heaven; secondly, Jātavedas was born from us.
Thirdly, he of manly mind was born in the waters. The pious man, kindling him, praises this eternal one.
We know your three forms, O Agni, in three ways; we know your stations distributed in many places. We know your supreme name that is hidden in secret; we know that spring from which you have come.
Manly-minded, I have kindled you within the waters, O ocean; man-beholding, I have kindled you, O Agni, in the lap of heaven.
In the third realm, the mighty ones have strengthened you as you stood upon the lap of the waters. Agni roared like the thundering sky, licking the earth and anointing the plants.
As soon as he was born, being kindled, he looked abroad; with his radiance he shines between the two worlds.
The noble upholder of glories, the supporter of riches, the bringer of inspired thoughts, the guardian of Soma;
the good Son of Strength, the King in the waters, shines forth at the forefront, kindled by the Dawns.
The banner of all, the germ of the world, he filled the two worlds, heaven and earth, at his birth.
Even the firm mountain he shattered as he went forth, when the five peoples sacrificed to Agni.
The desiring, purifying, wise messenger, the immortal Agni, has been established among mortals.
Bearing it aloft, he sends up his ruddy smoke, striving to reach the heavens with his bright flame.
Visible like a golden ornament, he has shone far and wide; his life is invincible, as he gleams with the splendor of beauty.
Through his vital powers, Agni became immortal when the prolific Dyaus brought him forth.
O Agni of auspicious luster, may he who today prepares for you a cake rich in ghee, O God—
Lead him further forward toward greater wealth and toward the favor bestowed by the gods, O youngest one.
Grant him a share in glorious renown, O Agni; grant him a share at every hymn being recited.
May he be dear to Sūrya and dear to Agni; may he prevail through what has been born and through what is yet to be born.
O Agni, day after day, the sacrificers have placed all desirable treasures within you.
Seeking wealth through you, the seekers have opened the cow-stall.
Agni, the benevolent friend of men, has been praised by the seers as Vaiśvānara, the guardian of Soma.
We invoke the benevolent Heaven and Earth; O gods, bestow upon us wealth with heroic sons.
The Hotṛ, born great, pervading the atmosphere, seated among men, has taken his place in the lap of the waters.
He who was established as the sustainer—may he, the protector of our bodies, ordain for you vital strengths and bestow riches.
Worshipping him in the gathering place of the waters, they followed his tracks like one seeking a lost animal.
Seeking him who was hidden in the cave with prostrations, the wise Bhr̥gus, longing for him, found him. Trita, the son of Vibhūvasu, searching for him, found him many times upon the head of the cow.
Born in the dwellings as one who increases prosperity, he becomes the youthful center of the luminous realm.

The eager ones, with prostrations, [establish] the delightful Hotṛ-priest, the leader of sacrifices, who guides the rites forward. They have made him the purifying steward of the people, establishing him among men as the bearer of oblations.

The foolish ones led forward the wise one—the great, victorious upholder of inspired thought, the breaker of forts—as they brought the child into the woods. They placed him there, whose beard is like a sacrificial ladle, who is like a steed neighing for wealth.
Trita, establishing himself in his dwellings, sat within the womb, enveloped.
From there, the friend of the people, the domestic lord, gathering them together, moves among men according to the law with his guiding restraints.
His are the fires, ageless, protectors of the household, purifying, with glowing smoke;
they are brilliant white, strengthening, restless, dwelling in the woods like winds, like Soma-drops.
Agni bears forth his inspired song with his tongue; through his wisdom, he proclaims the ordinances of the earth.
Men have established him as the purifying, joyous Hotṛ-priest, the most skilled in sacrifice, as he shines brightly.
Both Heaven and Earth, the Waters, Tvaṣṭṛ, and the Bhṛgus have brought forth this Agni with their powers.
Mātariśvan and the gods fashioned him, the first one worthy of praise, for man—the worshipful one.

You, whom the gods established as the bearer of oblations, you who are much-desired and worshipful among men—O Agni, bestow strength upon the singer during his course; for many glorious ones indeed seek the path of the gods.
We have grasped your right hand, O Indra, seeking wealth, O Lord of treasures, Lord of riches.
For we know you, O Hero, as the master of cattle; grant us wonderful, virile wealth. [He is] well-armed, well-aided, a good leader, the four-sea container of riches.

Grant us wealth that is worthy of celebration, praiseworthy, and of many boons— wealth that is wonderful, virile, and powerful. O Indra, grant us wealth that is accompanied by excellent prayer, favored by the gods, vast, deep, broad-based,
renowned among seers, fierce, and a subduer of adversaries— wealth that is wonderful and virile.

O Indra, grant us wonderful, bull-like wealth—winning booty, with inspired heroes, victorious, seizing riches, ever-increasing, and most skillful; O slayer of Dasyus and breaker of forts, grant us true wealth.
O Indra, grant us strength consisting of horses, chariots, and heroes, in hundreds and thousands.
Grant us a host of auspicious ones, with heroic sages, winners of light—a wondrous, bull-like wealth.
My prayer goes forth to Bṛhaspati, the sevenfold-knower, the sage whose thoughts are fixed on Truth;
he who is of the Aṅgiras clan and is to be approached with homage—grant us a wondrous, bull-like wealth.
My yearning messengers, these hymns of praise, go forth toward Indra, seeking his favor.
Touching the heart and uttered with the mind, O showerer of blessings, grant us wondrous and abundant wealth.
O Indra, grant us that which I ask of you: a vast dwelling, peerless among men.
May Heaven and Earth approve this; grant us wonderful, vigorous wealth.
I have become the ancient lord of riches; I win all treasures together. Men call upon me as they call a father; I distribute food to the one who offers oblations.
I am Indra, the dam; from Atharvan I took the cattle for Trita from the dragon.
I seized manly strength from the Dasyus, bestowing the cow-pens upon Dadhyanc and Mātariśvan.
For me Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned the iron thunderbolt; in me the gods concentrated their will.

My host is difficult to overcome like that of the Sun; I am [so] by the noble deed and by what must be done. With my arrow, I have struck down this cattle-rich, horse-rich, and gold-rich herd, along with the manure-pile.
I sharpen many thousands for the donor, since the Soma-pressing hymns have exhilarated me.

I am Indra; I have never been defeated in the contest for wealth, nor have I ever yielded to death at any time. Pressing the Soma, do not beg me for riches; O Pūrus, you shall not suffer harm in my friendship.
I, Indra, [overcame] these two who were snorting, those who made the thunderbolt their weapon for battle.
I struck down with my blow those who were challenging me, speaking firm words to those who offered homage while they themselves were without homage.
I alone am the one who overcomes; I overcome two, so what can three do? Like a threshing-floor, I strike down the many. Why do these enemies, who lack Indra, revile me?
I brought forth Atithigva for the sake of the Guṅgus; like food, I maintained him among the people as a subduer of Vṛtra.
Whether it was at the slaying of Parṇaya or at the killing of Karañja, I won renown in the great battle against Vṛtra.
Namī Sāpya submitted to me so that I might enjoy his nourishment; he sought cattle and established friendship with me once again.
When he brandished his bolt in the battles, I made him worthy of praise and hymns.

In one case Soma was seen within; the other, the guardian, makes himself manifest. Desiring to fight the bull with sharpened horns, he stood bound within the vast expanse, away from the malicious ones.
The god of the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Rudriyas—I do not violate the domain of the gods. They have fashioned me for auspicious power—unconquered, unsubdued, and invincible.
I bestow ancient wealth upon the singer; I shall make the sacred word (*brahman*) an increase for myself.
I have become the instigator for the sacrificer in every battle against the non-sacrificer; I am the witness in every fray.
Me, the creatures of heaven, earth, and the waters, have set up as the deity named Indra.
I have taken the two bay steeds, powerful and swift, moving in different directions; I have grasped the bold thunderbolt for the sake of strength.
I struck Atka with blows for the sake of the seer Kavi; I protected Kutsa with these aids of mine.
I, the slayer of Śuṣṇa, held back the weapon, so that the Dasyu should not seize the Aryan name.
Like a father, I subjected the Vetasus, Tugra, and Smadibha to Kutsa for his protection.
I was present at the sacrifice for the king when he brought forward his dear ones to win the prize and defy the bold.
I delivered Mṛgaya into the power of Śrutarvan, since he followed me in succession, seeking to know my ways.
I made Veśa bow down before Āyu; I delivered Paḍgr̥bhi into the hands of Savya.
I am he who, like the slayer of Vṛtra, shattered the Dāsa Navavāstva of the great chariot;
I, who brought to light the luminous realms in the far distance of the mid-air for him as he grew and expanded among men.
Borne onward with vigor by my swift, dappled steeds, I travel around the sun.
When the libation of Manu called me to his raiment, I drove away the Dāsa Āsa with my blows, making him a thing of the past.
I am the slayer of the seven Nahuṣas, more Nahuṣa-like than the Nahuṣas; by my might I made Turvaśa and Yadu famous.
By my power I brought low one who was stronger than strength, and I caused the ninety-nine Navavrādhas to prosper.
I, the bull, sustain the seven flowing rivers that run in haste upon the earth, over the furrows. I, of skillful wisdom, spread out the floods; through battle, I found a path for man’s desire.
I established in them that which not even the god Tvaṣṭṛ had established before—the radiant [light].
Desirable is the udder of the cows within their beautiful flanks; it is the honey of honey, the invigorating *āśira* mixed with Soma.
Thus has Indra, the bounteous one whose gifts are true, stirred the gods and men with his mighty deed.
All these [deeds] of yours, O Lord of Bay Horses, O Lord of Might, do they praise as swift and self-glorious.
Sing forth for the great one who rejoices in the soma-juice, for Viśvānara, the creator of all;
for Indra, whose battle-winning might, great fame, and manly valor both heaven and earth revere.
Even he, the heroic lord, praised and worthy of song for friendship, is Indra, such as I am, O man.
O Lord of the Good, you rejoice in all burdens, in deeds that win the prize, in the slaying of Vṛtra, and in the waters, O Hero.
Who are those men, O Indra, who strive for your refreshment, who seek your blissful and wealth-bestowing favor?
Who have urged you on toward heroic power, who in the waters, in the fertile fields, and in manly deeds?
O Indra, you have become great through our prayer; you have become worthy of sacrifice at all libations.
O Lord of all people, you are the shaker of men in every battle, and you are the most excellent counselor.
Now, as one superior, protect us, O seeker of sacrifice; the people know your great assistance.
May you indeed be free from decay; may you grow strong, for you have made all these libations effective.
You yourself, O Son of Strength, have established all these libations which you hold fast.
For your choice and for the maintenance of the law, there is the vessel, the sacrifice, the mantra, the sacred formulation, and the word raised up in praise.
O Sage, those who have offered prayers to you at the pressing, so that you may grant us wealth and treasures—
may they come forth through the path of your benevolence with a willing mind, in the exhilaration of the pressed Soma juice.
Great was that womb, firm was that covering, enveloped by which you entered the waters.
O Agni Jātavedas, you alone, the god, have beheld all your many forms in their various ways.
Who has seen me? Which one is that god who has surveyed my forms in their many ways? Where, O Mitra and Varuṇa, do all the fuel-sticks of Agni, which lead to the gods, abide?
RV 10.51.3: We sought you in many places, O Jātavedas, you who have entered into the waters and the plants, O Agni.
You, O Citrabhānu, Yama perceived as you were shining intensely from within the ten fingers.
RV 10.51.4: Fearing the office of the *hotṛ*, O Varuṇa, I fled, lest the gods should yoke me to that task.
My bodies have entered into many places; I am this Agni whom Naciketas [sought].
Come, O Manu, seeker of the gods and desirous of sacrifice; having prepared [the altar], do not remain in the darkness, O Agni.
Make the paths leading to the gods easy to travel; being well-disposed, carry the oblations.
Agni’s elder brothers pursued this goal as a charioteer follows the path.

Out of fear of that, O Varuṇa, I went far away; like a wild bull, I fled from the archer’s bowstring. We shall grant thee a life free from decay, O Agni, so that when thou art harnessed, O Jātavedas, thou shalt not come to harm among men.
Then, being well-disposed, O well-born one, carry to the gods their portion of the oblation.
Grant me the *prayāja* and *anuyāja* offerings exclusively, and give me a vigorous portion of the oblation.
May there be for us the fatness of the waters, the essence of the plants, and long life from Agni, O gods!
May the fore-offerings and the after-offerings be yours alone; may they be full of vigor and portions of the oblation.
O Agni, let this entire sacrifice be yours; let the four quarters bow down before you.
O All-Gods, instruct me how, having been chosen as the Hotar-priest and seated here, I shall perform my service according to the thought of Manu.
Declare to me my portion, how it is for you, and by which path I shall carry the oblation to you.
I have sat down as the Hotṛ, the most skilled in sacrifice; all the gods and the Maruts impel me.
Day after day, O Aśvins, the office of Adhvaryu belongs to you; the Brahman is kindled, and this is your oblation.
Who indeed is this Hotṛ of Yama? Whom do the gods intend to anoint?
Day after day, month after month, he is born; thus have the gods established him as the bearer of oblations.
Me, the gods have established as the bearer of oblations—me, who was cast away and wandered through many hardships.
May Agni, the wise one, arrange for us the sacrifice that has five paths, threefold, and seven threads.
O gods, I shall worship you for immortality and great heroism, so that I may create wide space for you.
May the thunderbolt be placed within the two arms of Indra; then he shall conquer all these hostile armies.
Three thousand, three hundred, and thirty-nine gods have worshipped Agni;
they have sprinkled him with clarified butter, they have strewn the sacrificial grass for him, and then they have seated him as the Hotṛ-priest.
He whom we sought in our mind has arrived—this one, the knower of the sacrifice, who understands its every part.
May he, the most skilled in sacrifice, worship for us among the gods; may he sit down as one who is close to us, even before us.
The Hotṛ-priest has been successful by his sitting down, the most skilled in sacrifice; may he look upon the well-placed offerings.
Let us sacrifice to the gods worthy of sacrifice; come, let us praise with clarified butter those who are worthy of praise.
May he today make our divine feast successful; we have found the secret tongue of the sacrifice.
He has come, fragrant and clothed in life, making our invocation of the gods auspicious today. May I today utter that first word of speech by which we gods may overcome the Asuras.
O eaters of strength, you who are worthy of sacrifice, may you five tribes enjoy my oblation!
May the five tribes enjoy my oblation—those born of the cow and those who are worthy of sacrifice! May the Earth protect us from what belongs to the earth!
May he protect us from the atmosphere and from heaven. Spinning out the thread, follow the light of the mid-world; guard the luminous paths prepared by wisdom.
Weave the web without flaw for the singers; become Manu and generate the divine race.

O ye who are worthy of Soma, fasten the axle-pins; prepare the thongs and weave the straps. Draw the chariot with its eight-seated seat from both sides, by which the gods brought [the bride] to her beloved.
The stony river flows; hold fast one another, arise, and cross over, O friends!
Right here we leave behind those who were unfriendly; may we cross over to auspicious strengths.

Tvaṣṭṛ, the most skillful in arts among the possessors of wisdom, bearing the vessels most propitious for the gods' drinking, now sharpens his axe of good metal, with which Etaśa, the Lord of Prayer, shall cut away [the obstacles].
O sages, truly sharpen now the axes wherewith you fashion the immortal;
O wise ones, make known the secret places by which the gods attained immortality. They placed the child within the womb, the calf upon the lap, with their secret mind and their tongue.
He, being well-disposed every day toward his tasks, wins the prize with his desire to conquer; he indeed secures victory.
O Maghavan, that fame of yours is great through your majesty, when the two worlds, struck with fear, invoked you.
You protected the gods and overcame the Dāsa’s power, since you, O Indra, bestowed aid upon this progeny.
When you strode forth, increasing in body and proclaiming your powers among the people, O Indra—was that a mere illusion?
Of those battles they speak of, you have found no enemy today, nor did you find one in the past. Who indeed among the seers before us has ever reached the limit of your entire greatness?
When you brought forth both mother and father together from your own body;
Four are your divine names, unassailable, belonging to you, the Mighty One. Verily, you know them all, O Maghavan, by which you performed your deeds.
You possess all treasures exclusively—those that are manifest and those that are hidden in secret.
O Maghavan, do not frustrate my desire; you are the director, O Indra, you are the giver. He who placed light within light, he who created honeyed things with honey.
Then a dear, powerful hymn was spoken by the composer of prayer to Indra from Bṛhaduktha.
Far away is that secret name, which the two terrified ones called upon you for the sake of vital strength.
You propped up the earth and the sky in the encounter, O Maghavan, shining brightly against your brother’s sons.
Great is that secret name, sought by many, by which you brought forth what has been and what is to be.
The five beloved tribes entered into that ancient light which was born as his own dear essence.
He filled the two worlds, the middle space, and the five classes of gods, seven by seven, according to their seasons.
With thirty-four forms he looks out in many ways, with a uniform light that is not subject to vows.
When you, O Dawn, shone forth as the first of the radiant ones, you brought forth the nourishment of nourishment.
That kinship of yours which is nearer than the further, and that great, singular sovereignty of yours, O Great One.
The grey-haired one has swallowed the moon as it sped along in the assembly of many, though it was still young.
Behold the poetic wisdom and the greatness of the god: he who was here yesterday has died today.
By his own power, the powerful, ruddy, fair-winged one—who is great and a hero from of old—remains unassailable.
Whatever he has willed is true, not in vain; he is the winner and the giver of desirable wealth.

Through these [powers] he has obtained manly strengths, by which the wielder of the thunderbolt grew mighty for the slaying of Vṛtra—the gods who, through the greatness of the rite being performed, were born by the power of the rite itself.
Performing deeds with his companion, possessing all vigor, warding off the ill-spoken, all-minded, and swift-conquering;
having drunk of the Soma and increasing from heaven, the hero blew away the Dasyus from the battle.
This is one light for you, and another beyond that; enter into union with the third light.
Be beautiful in the union with the body; be dear to the gods in the highest place of birth.
O vigorous one, may your body, leading your own body, bestow what is desirable upon us and grant protection to you.
Unharmed, for the support of the great gods, may you measure out your own light like [the sun] in heaven.
O Steed, with thy strength, go to the well-guiding waters; being well-guided, go to the hymn and go to heaven.
Being well-guided, follow the first true laws; being well-guided, follow the gods; being well-guided, follow thy flight.
By their greatness, even the fathers have attained lordship; the gods have placed wisdom within the gods.
They have encompassed all that they desired, and those [powers] which they sent forth have entered again into their bodies.
With their might, they have traversed the entire realm, measuring out the immeasurable ancient abodes.
They have established all beings within their bodies and have spread forth progeny in many directions.
In two ways the sons established the Asura who finds the light of heaven by their third deed;
the fathers placed their own offspring and the paternal heritage together within the lower worlds, like a stretched-out thread.
As if with a boat across the waters, they have passed through all difficulties toward the quarters of the earth with blessings.
Bṛhaduktha, by his greatness, placed his own offspring among those both near and far.
May we not stray from the path, O Indra; may we, possessing Soma, not be excluded from the sacrifice.
May no enemies stand against us.
May we obtain him who is offered, he who is the accomplisher of the sacrifice, whose thread is stretched out among the gods.
Now we invoke the mind with the Soma that is accompanied by the praise of men (nārāśaṃsa).
And with the hymns of the fathers...
May your mind return to you for the sake of will, for skill, and for life, so that you may long behold the sun.
May the Fathers and the divine folk grant us back our mind; may we be united with the company of the living. O Soma, we who bear our minds within our bodies abide in your law.
May we, possessing offspring, be united with you.
O Yama, son of Vivasvat, that mind of yours which has gone far away to Vaivasvata— we bring it back to you here, so that you may dwell and live.
That mind of yours which has gone far away to heaven or to earth— bring that back to you. That mind of yours which has gone far away to the four-cornered earth— bring that back to you.
RV_10.058.03.2: May that [be yours]...
RV_10.058.04.1: Since your mind has gone far away to the four quarters of space, RV_10.058.04.2: may that [be yours]...
When your mind went far away to the billowing ocean, that [mind] of yours [we bring back].
When your mind went far away to the rays of light and the slopes, that [mind] of yours [we bring back].
RV_10.058.06.2: That [breath] of yours... RV_10.058.07.1:
That mind of yours which has gone far away into the waters or into the plants— RV_10.058.07.2: That [mind] of yours...

O Sūrya, that mind of yours which has gone far away to the sun or to the dawn— bring that back to us. O Sūrya, that mind of yours which has gone far away to the great mountains— bring that back to us.
RV_10.058.09.2: That [is yours]... RV_10.058.10.1: That mind of yours which has gone far away to this entire world— RV_10.058.10.2: That [is yours]...
When your mind has gone far away to distant realms beyond, let it return to you... When your mind has gone far away to both what has been and what is to be, let it return to you.

RV 10.58.12.2: That [is] yours... RV 10.59.1.1: May life be further extended anew, like two skillful charioteers standing upon their chariot. RV 10.59.1.2: Then Cyavāna, through his own power, moved far beyond his former state.
Let us now prepare a treasury for wealth and food, and perform many deeds of glorious renown.
May our singer rejoice in all these things; may a most excellent liberation come to us from afar.
May we overcome our enemies through manly deeds, as the heaven towers over the earth and the mountains rise above the plains.
Our singer has perceived all these things; may a happy exit be granted for the further journey.
O Soma, do not deliver us over to death; may we yet behold the rising sun.
May our old age be established by the days; may a happy exit be granted for the further journey.
O Asunīti, maintain the mind within us; prolong our lifespan so that we may live.
Grant us delight in the sight of the sun; cause our bodies to grow strong with clarified butter.
O Asunīti, bestow upon us again the faculty of sight and again the breath of life; grant us here the enjoyment of existence.
May we long behold the sun rising; O Anumati, be gracious to us for our well-being.
May the earth give back our life-breath to us, may the divine sky, and may the mid-air give it back. May Soma restore our body to us, and may Pūṣan restore the path that is our well-being.
May Heaven and Earth, the two young mothers of Truth, grant well-being to Subandhu.
May they carry away whatever blemish there is; O Heaven and Earth, remove the stain from us, and let nothing whatsoever afflict you.
The healing medicines descend from heaven in twos and threes.
May they carry away the solitary one who wanders upon the earth; may Heaven and Earth carry away all sin and impurity. May nothing whatsoever cause you distress.
Drive hither the oxen that draw the wagon which has brought the goods from the Uśīnaras. May they carry away the solitary one who wanders upon the earth;
may Heaven and Earth carry away all sin and impurity. May nothing whatsoever cause you distress.
We have come bearing homage to the person of brilliant aspect, praised among the great ones. To the peerless, bestowing, brilliant, and ever-advancing chariot.
Seek as your portion the Lord of the Good,
he who, armed with the spear, has stood over the people like a buffalo,
and even without the spear, is victorious in battle.
In whose service Ikṣvāku prospers like a wealthy man, O Marāyī,
and in whom the five tribes flourish as if in heaven—
O Indra, uphold the sovereignty among those who are peerless, who possess chariots and fine horses.
Like the sun in the sky for all to see,
you have harnessed the two ruddy steeds from the waters of Agastya. O King, you have stepped down upon the Paṇis, all those who offer no gifts.
This is the mother, this is the father; this life-giving power has arrived.
This is your creeping forth; come out for the sake of Subandhu.
Just as they bind the yoke with a leather thong for the sake of support, so do you emerge.
Thus he has supported your mind for life, not for death, but for safety. Just as this great earth supports these trees,
so has he supported your mind for life, not for death, but for safety.
From Yama, the son of Vivasvat, I have brought back the spirit of Subandhu, that he may live and not die, and that he may attain safety.
The wind blows downward; the sun shines downward.
Downward the cow yields her milk; let your malady go downward.
This hand of mine is blessed; this hand of mine is more blessed. This hand of mine possesses all healing powers; this is the one whose touch is auspicious.
Thus, with skill and power within the battle, the one of praised speech offered this formidable prayer to Rudra.
When he, acting as the most generous one, brought his parents across at Paktha, he slew the seven Hotṛ-priests.
He, Cyavāna, seeking to win for the sake of giving and deception, measured out the altar with the *sūda* offerings.
Tūrvayāṇa, whose speech is most praised, has poured forth the seed like a flood, providing protection.
At whose invocations you two, rushing forward with power, win the sharp inspired songs like thoughts;
he, the one of many manly deeds, who with his arrows has filled the quarters with his hand.
When the dark one settled among the ruddy cows, I invoke you two, O Aśvins, sons of Heaven.

Come to my sacrifice; come to my food, you who have won the prize and do not forget your firm resolve. He whose heroic deed has spread wide, he, the manly one, has now accomplished what was to be done.
Then again, the invincible one drew out that which had been carried away from the maiden’s daughter;

when the deed was to be done in the midst of the encounter, the father, acting according to his desire toward the young woman, they both released their minds and cast forth the seed as they went apart, it being poured into the womb of the well-fashioned work.
When the father begat his own daughter, uniting with her upon the earth, he poured forth his seed.
The wise ones, seeking the gods, generated the sacred word and fashioned Vāstoṣpati, the guardian of the vows.
Like a bull, he cast forth foam in the battle; then, with unwavering mind, he went forward and struck down the enemy.
Like a swift-footed courser, he has come hither; like a cow returning home, the dappled mares have seized him.
Like a bearer of the people, he hastens; like one who was naked, he has sat down by Agni at the udder.
He wins the fuel, and he wins the prize; he was born as the sustainer, striving with conquering might.
Swiftly did the Navagvas come to the friendship of Kanāyā, proclaiming the *ṛta* and the union with *ṛta*.
Those who, possessing double strength, approached the guardian of the herd—being liberal givers—they milked from the unshakable source.
Swiftly did they seek the new friendship of Kanāyā; like a gift, they sped toward the seed, furthering the *ṛta*.
That pure wealth which they offered to you from the milk of the ever-yielding cow;
when he wakes up later with his cattle, the speaker, not withholding his words, says: "The poets, through the excellence of their wealth, have unerringly encompassed all riches for the sake of food."
Then indeed his attendants arrived; sitting in many places, they sought to break through the stronghold of Nārṣada.
The invincible one discovered that which was hidden in the cave of Śuṣṇa, who had many offspring.
His name is *Bharga*, and the gods who dwell in the triple-seated abode are his.
Agni indeed is by name Jātavedas; hear us, O Hotṛ, the guileless Hotṛ of Ṛta.

And may those two radiant Nāsatyas, the sons of Rudra, be praised for me to worship, O Indra—those who, like Manu, delighting in him whose sacrificial grass is trimmed, are joyful and worthy of sacrifice among the people, provided with the oblation of the heart.
This king has been praised; he is the worshipper, the creator, the seer who spreads out the waters, having himself as his bridge.
He made Kakṣīvat tremble; he made Agni tremble, like the swiftly running wheel-rim of a racing horse.
He, the doubly-related son of Vitaraṇa, the sacrificer, milked the bountiful cow Sabardhu for the sake of the draught.
When I encompass Mitra and Varuṇa with hymns, and Aryaman with the highest protections;

then the patron, kinsman of that [sacrifice], bestows his thought upon heaven—Nābhānediṣṭha, who speaks out with longing. This is our supreme kinship, or indeed my own; how many others have there been after him?

This is my navel; here is my dwelling place; these are my gods; this is all that is within me. Twice-born indeed am I, the first-born of Cosmic Order (Ṛta); as she was being born, the Cow milked this out.
Then, among these [beings], the delightful, radiant, and far-reaching messenger, who moves in two ways and dwells in the woods, rests.

When the upright line [of flames] roars like a child, the mother has swiftly brought forth the firm strengthener. Then the cows went toward the approach of the maiden, following after the breath of some one.
Hear us, O possessor of splendid wealth; come to us for the increase of Āśvaghna with your gracious truths.
So then, O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, Lord of men, recognize us for the sake of great wealth.
Protect our wealthy patrons and guard the wise singers; O Lord of the bay horses, preserve those who are blameless under your protection.
And when the two Kings, the swift-moving and the one who hastens to the singer, go forth in the search for cattle, they move with speed.
He has become the most beloved sage among them; he has carried them across and shall carry them further.
Now, for the sake of the prosperity of this noble one, we approach him with spontaneous hymns; we seek that very thing from him.
He is the swift son, the steed; you are the inspired singer in the winning of glory.
If, for the sake of your friendship with us, you have accepted this hymn for the host with reverence— he in whom all songs are united, who bestows many swift paths for the sake of true bounty—

then he, being praised by the waters, accompanied by the gods, and well-allied through homage and well-spoken hymns, shall grow strong through our recitations and words; for now indeed, let him partake of the milk of the ruddy cow.
O worshipful gods, may you indeed become great and of one accord for our protection—

ye who, moving apart, brought us strength, and who stand as wise perceivers of all. Those who were consecrated by sacrifice and the sacrificial fee have attained the friendship of Indra and immortality.
May there be prosperity for you, O Aṅgirases; accept this man, O wise ones.
O Fathers, you who drove forth the wealth consisting of cattle, and by the Eternal Law broke open the enclosure in a full year— May long life be yours, O Aṅgirases; accept this man, O wise ones.
They who by *ṛta* caused the sun to ascend in heaven and spread out the earth, the mother;
may you, O Aṅgirases, possess good progeny. Accept me, O wise ones, as a descendant of Manu.
This man speaks sweetly in the center of your house; O seers, sons of gods, hear this!
O wise ones, let there be the Subrahmaṇyā for you, O Aṅgirases; accept the descendant of Manu.
These seers are indeed Virūpas, they whose inspiration is profound;
these sons of the Aṅgirases were born from Agni.
Those who were born from Agni, the multiform ones from heaven—
Navagva, Nudaśagva, the best of the Aṅgirases— he is honored together with the gods.
With Indra as their ally, the worshippers have released the stall full of cattle and horses.
To me who gives a thousand, the eight-eared ones have won glory among the gods.
May this Manu now be born; may he grow like a young shoot, he who immediately bestows for a gift a thousand and a hundred horses.
No one can reach him, as if grasping the ridges of heaven;
the sacrificial fee of Sāvarṇya has spread out like a river. Moreover, two Dāsas, well-disposed and rich in cattle, wait upon him to serve.
That Ustara and Turva have bestowed upon me—may the leader, the giver of thousands, not be harmed; may Manu go forth with the sun, and may the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) come hither.
O gods, may they prolong the life of Sāvarṇi, in whom we, unwearied, have won the prize.
Those who, from afar, desire kinship, being well-disposed toward Manu’s progeny and the offspring of Vivasvat;
those gods who sit upon the sacred grass of Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa—may they speak in our favor.
For all your names, O gods, are worthy of homage and adoration, and you are indeed worthy of sacrifice.
You who are born from Aditi, from the waters, and from the earth—listen here to our call!
For whom the Mother pours forth honeyed milk and the primordial nectar, O Dyaus, Aditi, and you of mountain-like strength;
Those Ādityas, whose vigor is the hymn, who bear the bull, and who are well-disposed—rejoice after them for our well-being!
Beholding men, never blinking, and worthy of worship, the gods have attained great immortality.
With chariots of light, possessing the power of serpents and free from sin, they clothe themselves in the height of heaven for our well-being.
Those sovereign lords, who prosper the sacrifice and have come hither, have established their unassailable dwelling in the sky.
I invite them with reverence and well-fashioned hymns—the great Ādityas and Aditi—for our well-being.
O All-Gods, who among men offers you a hymn that you may enjoy? You, O gods, are the ones who attend to man.
O you of mighty birth, who shall prepare for you a sacrifice that is sufficient, so that he may carry us across distress to well-being?

To whom Manu, with kindled fire, first offered the oblation with his mind through the seven priests—O Ādityas, grant us fearless protection; make our paths easy to traverse and fair for our well-being.
They who rule over the world, the wise ones, who take thought for all that is stationary and all that moves.
O Gods, deliver us today from the sin we have committed and that which we have not yet committed, for our well-being.

In battles, we invoke Indra, who is easy to call upon, the deliverer from distress, and the divine host who performs good deeds. We invoke Agni, Mitra, Varuṇa, Bhaga, Heaven and Earth, and the Maruts for our gain and for our well-being.

We would ascend for our well-being the Earth, the good protector, the Heaven free from blemish, Aditi who provides excellent shelter and excellent guidance—the divine ship with fair oars, sinless and leakless. O all you holy ones, speak in our favor for our protection; save us from the malice of the evil-minded and from injury.
With our truthful invocation of you, O gods, may we call upon you who hear us, for protection and for well-being.
Drive away sickness, drive away all lack of offerings, and keep far from us the ill-will of the malicious man who seeks to harm us.
O gods, keep enmity far from us; grant us wide shelter for our well-being.
Unharmed, that mortal prospers in every way; he is multiplied with offspring according to the cosmic law (*dharman*).

Whom you, O Ādityas, lead with your excellent guidance across all difficulties for his well-being—whom you gods protect in the struggle for booty, whom you Maruts protect in the battle for heroes when the prize is set.
O Indra, may we mount for our well-being the early-faring chariot that wins booty and brings no harm.
May you grant us well-being on the paths and in the desert wastes; well-being in the waters, in the assembly, and in the light-filled realm.
Grant us well-being in the wombs of our progeny, and well-being for the sake of wealth, O Maruts!
This blessing indeed is the best on the distant path; full of wealth, it comes toward us with protection.
May she protect us at home and in the forest; may she be easy of access and a divine guardian.
Thus has the wise son of Plati magnified you all, O Ādityas and Aditi.
The lords, the heroes, have been praised with an immortal song by the celestial folk.
How, on the journey of the gods, shall we invoke the name of which one among those who hear our call? Who will be gracious? Which one will grant us joy? Which one will turn toward us with his aid?
The powers of will act as wills; thoughts within the hearts long for them as seekers; they fly from every direction.

No other comforter is found besides these; among the gods, my desires have been set upon them. O men, with my song I honor Pūṣan, the one who cannot be hidden, and Agni kindled by the gods, for their praise.

Sūrya and Māsa, Candramas, Yama in heaven, Trita, Vāta, Uṣas, Aka, and the Aśvins—how does the poet, the one with many heroes, praise them? By what song, by what well-fashioned hymns, is Bṛhaspati magnified?
May Aja Ekapād hear our call, and may Ahi Budhnya, with the singers who are easy to invoke, listen at our invocation.
At the birth of Dakṣa, in his proclaimed ordinance, you seek to win over the two kings, Mitra and Varuṇa.
Aryaman, whose path is unsurpassed and who possesses many chariots, acts as the sevenfold priest among diverse races.
May all those swift steeds, who hear our invocation and run with great speed, hear our call.
They who, like winners of a thousand at the winning of the prize, have by their own power brought great wealth together in battles.
With hymns of praise, bring Vāyu, who yokes his chariot, and Purandhi, and Pūṣan, for the sake of friendship.
For they, being of one mind and one thought, follow the will and the power of the god Savitṛ.
The thrice-seven flowing rivers, the great waters, the forest trees, the mountains, and Agni we invoke for aid;
Kṛśānu, the archers, Tiṣya, and Rudra—the most Rudrian among the Rudras—we call to our common dwelling.
May Sarasvatī, Sarayu, and Sindhu with their billows, and the great, mighty rivers, come with their protection.
O divine Waters, mothers, makers of things ready, flow for us with ghee, milk, and honey; sing our praise!
And may the Mother Bṛhaddivā hear our word, and Tvaṣṭṛ, the father, together with the gods and their wives.
May R̥bhukṣan, Vāja, Rathaspati, and Bhaga—the joyous one worthy of praise—protect us who labor in worship.
Delightful to behold like a dwelling rich in food, auspicious is the praise of the Rudras, the Maruts.
May we be glorious among the people through our cattle; O ever-present gods, may we always be united with nourishment.
O Maruts, Indra, and gods—Varuṇa, Mitra—you have bestowed this prayer upon me.
Make her swell with milk like a cow; will you not carry our songs upon your chariot?
O Maruts, will you not surely take heed of us, your kinsmen?
May Aditi grant us that kinship at the very navel where we first come together; there may she establish for us a bond free from confusion.
For those two, Heaven and Earth, the great divine Mothers, worthy of sacrifice by their very birth, have come here from this place to the gods.
Both of them sustain both worlds with their supports, and together with the Fathers, they pour forth many nourishing foods.
This Hotrā, Bṛhaspati, whose wisdom is most excellent, reaches every desirable thing through his tireless devotion.
RV 10.64.15: Where the pressing-stone, extracting the honey, is raised loudly, there the wise ones have caused it to resound with their inspired hymns.

RV 10.64.16: Thus the seer, possessing many heroes, knowing the cosmic order (*ṛta*), desiring wealth and longing for riches, has here—through hymns and inspired thoughts—the sage (*vipra*) nourished the celestial generations of the clan.
Thus [spoke] the son of Plateḥ...
Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Vāyu, Pūṣan, and Sarasvatī, acting in harmony;
the Ādityas, Viṣṇu, the Maruts, the lofty Heaven, Soma, Rudra, Aditi, and Brahmaṇaspati.
Indra and Agni, lords of the virtuous, impelled by each other in the slayings of Vṛtra, dwell together in one abode;
with their vast might they have filled the mid-air. Soma, adorned with clarity, stirs up their greatness.
For I, the knower of Truth, offer hymns of praise to those great and unassailable ones, who increase the Truth.
May those who bestow wonderful wealth within the waters, the ocean-like expanse, grant us gifts for our glorification; may they be well-disposed toward us.
With their might, they have propped up the sun, the mid-air, the luminous realms, heaven and earth, and the broad ground.
Like nourishing powers, these gods—generous givers and wise patrons—glorify you and are praised by men.
Bestow gifts upon Mitra and Varuṇa, the two sovereign kings who, with their own mind, never falter toward the worshipper.
Their lofty domain shines by the power of Law; they have encompassed both heaven and earth as their support.
She, the cow, who goes around the path to the appointed place, yielding her milk, follows her laws from afar.
She, speaking forth for Varuṇa the donor, has offered with oblation to the gods and to Vivasvat.
Dwelling in heaven, fire-tongued, increasers of Truth, they sit pondering the womb of Truth.
Having propped up the sky, they have brought the waters by their might; having generated the sacrifice, they have measured out its body.
The two parents dwelling around, born of old, abide together in the same home in the womb of *ṛta*.
Heaven and Earth, of one law, swell with ghee-rich milk for Varuṇa, the mighty bull.
Parjanya and Vāta, the bulls who pour forth moisture; Indra, Vāyu, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman.
We invoke the gods, the Ādityas, and Aditi—those who are on earth, those who are in heaven, and those who are in the waters.
We call upon Tvaṣṭṛ, Vāyu, and the Ṛbhus who are honored; the two divine Hotṛ-priests, and Uṣas for our well-being. For prosperity, we seek Bṛhaspati, the wise devourer of Vṛtra, Indriya, and Soma.
They generated the sacred prayer, cattle, horses, plants, forest trees, the earth, the mountains, and the waters;
they raised up the sun in heaven, O bounteous ones, releasing the laws of the Āryas over the earth.
O Aśvins, you delivered Bhujyu from distress; you restored Śyāva, the son of Vadhrimatī.
You gave the youthful Vimada his bride; you restored Viṣṇāpū to Viśvaka.

May Pāvīravī, Tanitṛ, Aja-Ekapād, the Sustainer of Heaven, Sindhu, and the Waters of the ocean hear my words. May all the gods, together with Sarasvatī, with our prayers, and with Purandhī, listen to my speech.

May all the gods, together with their insights and wisdom, the immortal ones who know the cosmic order (*ṛta*) and are worthy of worship from Manu— may they, who bestow gifts, who protect us, who have found the light of heaven, and who delight in the heavenly song, graciously accept this prayer and hymn. Vasiṣṭha has praised the immortal gods who stand over all the worlds.
May they grant us wide-striding space today; do you ever protect us with your blessings.
I invoke for our well-being the gods of great renown, the light-makers who are wise in the sacrifice.
They have increased further by their all-knowing power—the immortals, led by Indra, who strengthen the cosmic order (*ṛta*).

Impelled by Indra and directed by Varuṇa, those who have attained a share of the light of the sun—within the host of Maruts, in the assembly, let us fix our thought; in the gathering of the bounteous, the wise have generated the sacrifice.
May Indra with the Vasus protect our household, and may Aditi with the Ādityas grant us shelter.
May Rudra, the god, together with the Rudras, be gracious to us; may Tvaṣṭṛ, along with the divine women, quicken us for our well-being.

Aditi, Heaven and Earth, the great Cosmic Order (Ṛta), Indra and Viṣṇu, the Maruts, and the lofty Sky—these gods we invoke for protection: the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, and Savitṛ of wondrous deeds.

Sarasvat with his insights, Varuṇa whose laws are firm, Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, the mighty Vāyu, and the Aśvins—these immortal ones, creators of sacred prayer, possessors of all wealth, may they grant us a triple-layered protection from distress.
May the sacrifice be potent; may the worthy of worship be potent; may the gods be potent, and the preparers of the oblation be potent.
O Bulls, Heaven and Earth are observers of the Eternal Order; Parjanya is the Bull, and the singers of praise are Bulls.
O Agni and Soma, you Bulls, for the winning of booty—I invoke you, the highly lauded Bulls.
May those two Bulls, who have been impelled by the sacrifice to the gods, extend to us a triple-layered protection.
The Kṣatriyas of firm vows, who perfect the sacrifice, dwell in the lofty heavens; they are the ornaments of the rites.
The priests of the fire-offering, seekers of Truth and free from guile, released the waters in the conquest of Vṛtra.
Generating heaven and earth according to their laws, they brought forth the waters, the plants, and the trees worthy of sacrifice.
The gods have filled the mid-air and the heavens for our protection; they have fashioned their own bodies according to their will.

May the upholders of heaven, the Ṛbhus with skillful hands, Vāta and Parjanya of the thundering bull, the waters, and the plants further our prayers. May Bhaga, Rāti, and the prize-winning steeds come to my invocation.
The ocean, the rivers, the dust, the mid-air, the one-footed unborn, the thunder, and the flood;
may Ahibudhnya hear my words, and may all the gods and the wise ones be mine.
May we be yours, O men, for the feast of the gods; lead our sacrifice forward with success.
O Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus, you bounteous givers, quicken these prayers being recited.
The two divine Hotṛ-priests, the first appointed, follow the path of Truth with perfect skill.
We pray to the Lord of the Field, our neighbor, and to all the immortal gods who never fail.

The Vasiṣṭhas have uttered their speech like fathers; being invoked by the gods, they act like seers for our well-being. Like affectionate kinsmen, the gods have come to our desire and shaken down wealth upon us.
Vasiṣṭha has praised the immortal gods...
Our father discovered this seven-headed, lofty hymn, born of the Eternal Order (*ṛta*). The son of all people, Ayāsya, brought it forth while reciting the liturgy for Indra.
Proclaiming the Truth, meditating on the straight path, the sons of Heaven, the heroes of the Asura, [have done so].
The Aṅgirases, establishing the inspired singer as their station, conceived the first foundation of the sacrifice.
Like swans, with their loudly crying companions, they cast off their stone-made bonds; Bṛhaspati, calling out toward the cows, praised them and sang aloud, knowing them well.
With two [steps] he helped [them], with one [step] he drove the cows that stood hidden behind the dam of falsehood.

Bṛhaspati, seeking light in the darkness, uncovered the cows; he brought forth the three [worlds]. Having shattered the western stronghold, he cut through the three [fortresses] together from the ocean.
Bṛhaspati found the dawn, the sun, the cow, and the light, like the thundering sky. Indra, with a roar as if with his hand, split Vala, the guardian of the milch-cows.
Seeking the milk-mixture with those whose hands were anointed with sweat, he made the Paṇi weep and stole away the cows.
With his true, radiant, and booty-seeking companions, he split open the enclosure of the cows.
Brahmaṇaspati, with his bull-like, boar-like companions who sweat from the heat of the ritual vessel, distributed the wealth.
With a truthful mind, they, seeking the cows, impelled the Lord of Cows with their prayers.
Bṛhaspati, with those who drink away mutual faults and with his own yoked companions, released the ruddy cows upward.
Increasing him with auspicious hymns in the assembly, they [approached] him like a roaring lion.
In the struggle for heroes, in every battle, may we rejoice after the bull Bṛhaspati, the victorious one.
When he won booty of every form and ascended to the highest dwellings in heaven,
we, being many and bearing light in our mouths, magnified the bull Bṛhaspati.
Make our prayer true, O Giver of Life; for even the lowly you protect with your own aids.
Let all adversaries fall behind us; hear this, O Heaven and Earth, you who pervade all things!
With his greatness, Indra split asunder the head of the great surging Arbuda.
He slew the serpent and set free the seven rivers; O Heaven and Earth, protect us with the gods!
Like birds swimming in the water, guarding themselves, they cry out like the thundering of clouds; like waves breaking from the mountains, the hymns of praise have roared toward Bṛhaspati in joy.
Approaching with the kine, the Aṅgiras has led Aryaman away like Bhaga.

Like Mitra among the people, he anoints the husband and wife; like Bṛhaspati, he anoints the swift steeds for the race. They are excellent wives, radiant, desirable, golden-hued, and of blameless form.

Bṛhaspati, having forced his way from the mountains, [released] the cows as if [winnowing] barley from the winnowing-baskets. Sprinkling the source of the nectar of Truth, he cast down the light of the sun like a torch from heaven.
Bṛhaspati, lifting up the cows from the rock, split the earth as one strips the bark from a tree with water.

With light he drove away the darkness from the mid-air; like the wind blowing away the *śīpāla* plant from the water, Bṛhaspati, having seized Vala, drove out the cows as the wind drives away the clouds.
When Bṛhaspati shattered the strength of the reviling Vala with his fire-heated hymns.
As with teeth one takes up what has been surrounded by the tongue, Bṛhaspati has made manifest the hidden treasures of the rays of light.
For Bṛhaspati knew that secret name of these lowing ones which was hidden in the dwelling place;
like a bird breaking open its egg, he himself brought forth the rays from the mountain.
They beheld the honey fastened within a stone, like a fish dwelling in shallow water;
Bṛhaspati, having split it open with his roar, drew it forth as one draws a cup from a tree.
He found the Soma, he found the sun, he found the fire; with his song of praise, he drove away the darkness.
Bṛhaspati stripped Vala, who had the form of a cow, of his marrow as if from a jointless bone. Like forests robbed of their leaves by winter frost, Vala lamented for his cows because of Bṛhaspati.
He performed an act that could not be imitated nor repeated, since the sun and moon rise in alternation.
The fathers adorned the sky with stars, as one adorns a dark horse with golden ornaments.
They placed darkness in the night and light in the day; Bṛhaspati split the mountain and found the cattle.
We have performed this homage to the cloud-born god who repeatedly roars after many [days].
May Bṛhaspati bestow upon us vital strength through cattle, through horses, and through heroes who are true men.
Auspicious is the sight of Agni Vadhryaśva; his guidance is excellent, and his approaches are most delightful.
When the clans of Sumitra kindle him at the forefront, he, offered with clarified butter, awakes and flashes forth in brilliance.
Clarified butter is the strengthener of Agni Vadhryaśva; clarified butter is his food, clarified butter is his delight.
Offered with clarified butter, he has spread himself far and wide; he shines like the sun, having clarified butter as his libation.
O Agni, that face of yours which Manu and Sumitra kindled—that very same one has been kindled anew.
As such, shine forth with wealth; enjoy our songs; grant us strength and bestow renown upon us here.
O Agni, you whom Vadhryaśva, having been previously entreated, kindled, do you take pleasure in this [offering].
Be the protector of our household and the guardian of our bodies; protect this gift of yours which is ours.
Be glorious, O son of Vadhryaśva, and our protector; let not the hostility of men overcome you.
Like a bold hero, a shaker of foes, yet a good friend, I shall now proclaim the name of the son of Vadhryaśva.
You have won together the treasures of the plains and the mountains; you have conquered the Dāsa and Ārya enemies.
Like a bold hero, a shaker of the people, O Agni, may you overcome those who attack us.
This Agni has a long thread, great oxen, a thousand stallions, and a hundred hymns; he is skillful and resplendent.
Being polished by men among the radiant ones, he shines brightly among the well-disposed who seek the gods.
In thee, O Jātavedas, is the cow easy to milk, yielding her bounty like one who never fails, ever-flowing in abundance.
Thou, O Agni, art kindled by men who possess sacrificial gifts, by the well-disposed Sumitras who seek the gods.
Even the immortal gods themselves, O Jātavedas, have proclaimed thy greatness, O son of Vadhryaśva.

When the human tribes came together in assembly, you, O Agni, conquered with the men who were strengthened by you. Like a father carrying his son on his lap, Vadhryaśva served you, O Agni; and you, O youngest one, taking pleasure in his fuel, overthrew even those who were previously most powerful. Constantly, through the men who have pressed the Soma, Agni has conquered the enemies of Vadhryaśva.
O you of wondrous luster, you have burned down even one who was common; you have shattered even the one who grew strong while increasing his power.

This Agni of Vadhryaśva is the slayer of Vṛtra, kindled from of old, to be invoked with reverent speech. O Vadhryaśva, trample upon our enemies, whether they be unrelated or related, and upon those who are arrogant.

O Agni, enjoy this fuel of mine; welcome with delight the ladle dripping with ghee at the place of the *iḷā*. Rise up, O you of noble will, upon the summit of the earth during the auspiciousness of the days, for the sacrifice to the gods.
May Narāśaṃsa come here as the foremost of the gods, with his horses of every form.
Upon the path of Truth, with reverence, the most divine one has prepared the sacrificial food for the gods. Men, possessing oblations, evermore entreat Agni for the office of messenger.
With most-swift horses and a well-rolling chariot, bring the gods here so that you may sit as the Hotṛ priest.
May the god-loved sacrificial grass spread out; may it extend crosswise and lengthwise, becoming fragrant for us.
O divine *barhis*, with a mind free from malice, worship the gods according to their desire, with Indra as their chief.
Touch the very summit of heaven, or expand further according to the measure of the earth.

O longing Doors, by your greatness, hold fast the great divine chariot, you who desire the chariot. May the two goddesses, Dawn and Night, the well-fashioned daughters of Heaven, sit down in their appointed place. May the desiring gods sit upon your wide, auspicious lap, O longing ones.
Upright is the pressing-stone; the great fire is well-kindled; the dear abodes are in the lap of Aditi.
O two chief priests, most wise officiants at this sacrifice, bestow upon us wealth through your worship.
O three goddesses, sit upon this wide sacrificial grass; we have prepared for you a pleasant seat.
Like Manu, may the goddess Iḷā, whose footsteps are anointed with ghee, enjoy the well-placed sacrifice and the oblations.
O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, whatever beauty you have brought forth, since you became the companion of the Aṅgirases;
as one who knows the way, do you, O giver of wealth, rich in jewels, desiring it, sacrifice at the path of the gods.

O Lord of the Forest, having bound [the victim] with a cord, bring it to the path of the gods, you who are wise. May the god make it savory and prepare the oblations; may Heaven and Earth protect my invocation. O Agni, bring Varuṇa for our sacrifice, and Indra from heaven, and the Maruts from the mid-air.
Let all the worshipful ones sit upon the sacred grass; let the immortal gods rejoice in the *svāhā*!

O Bṛhaspati, that which was the first beginning of speech, when they sent it forth, bestowing names—whatever was their most excellent and faultless essence, that, hidden in the secret cave, was made manifest through their love.
Where the wise, purifying speech with their mind like flour through a sieve, have fashioned it; there friends recognize their friendships. A blessed sign is placed upon their speech.
By means of sacrifice they followed the track of speech; they found it entered into the seers.
Having brought her hither, they have established her in many places; the seven singers celebrate her together.
And one, though seeing, has not perceived Speech; and one, though hearing, has not heard her.
But to another she has revealed her body, like a loving wife for her husband, well-adorned.
Moreover, they say that he drinks deeply in friendship; they do not urge him on even in contests for prizes.
He wanders with the barrenness of a spell, having heard speech that is without fruit and without flower.
He who has abandoned his companion, the one who knows the truth—of him there is no share even in speech.
If he hears him, he hears in vain, for he does not know the path of righteous action. Friends possessed of eyes and ears have become unequal in their mental speed.
Some are like ponds reaching to the mouth or the armpits; others appear as if they have bathed in them.
When Brahmins, as friends, perform the sacrifice together upon the impulses of the mind fashioned by the heart—on this very point they distinguish themselves through their insights;
the Brahmins move about, ascending to the heights. But these who neither go toward us nor away from us, who are neither true Brahmins nor those who prepare the Soma—[they are excluded].
RV 10.71.9: These [fools], having resorted to evil speech, spin out their web like spiders, lacking true understanding.
RV 10.71.10: All friends rejoice in the arrival of the glorious one, the conqueror in the assembly, their companion.
He is the remover of their sin, the winner of nourishment; indeed, he is prepared for the contest.
One, having nourished it, sits chanting the growth of the *ṛc*s; another sings the *gāyatra* song upon the *śakvarī* verses.
One speaks as a *brahmán* the knowledge of all that has been born; and another measures out the proportions of the sacrifice.
Now let us proclaim with inspired praise the births of the gods.
When the hymns are being recited, he who may behold [this] in a later age—
Brahmaṇaspati forged these together like a smith;
in the earliest age of the gods, existence was born from non-existence.
In the first age of the gods, being was born from non-being;
then the quarters of space were born after that, from Utānapad. Bhūḥ was born from Utānapad, and from Bhūḥ the quarters of space were born.
Dakṣa was born from Aditi; from Dakṣa, Aditi was born in turn. For Aditi was born, O Dakṣa, she who is your daughter.
After her, the gods were born, the auspicious ones whose kinship is with immortality.
O Gods, when you stood there in the waters, firmly grasped together, then, as if dancers were dancing, the thick dust was driven away.
O Gods, when, like ascetics, you caused the worlds to swell.
There you brought forth the sun, which was hidden within the ocean.
Eight were the sons of Aditi who were born from her own body;
with seven she approached the gods, but she cast Mārtāṇḍa away.
With her seven sons, Aditi went forth to the ancient age;
for the sake of progeny, she brought Mārtāṇḍa back from death. You were born fierce for victorious power, delightful, most mighty, and full of great pride.
The Maruts indeed strengthened Indra there, when the Mother bore the Hero as her most bounteous gift.
Though seated in malice, even Pr̥śni was moved by the gods; they have greatly increased Indra with their many praises.
Like embryos confined within a covering, they emerged from the darkness of the deep pit.
Lofty are your feet when you stride forth; the strengths (vāja) that are here have increased you.
O Indra, you held a thousand hyenas in your mouth; you turned back the two Aśvins.
Swiftly you go to the sacrifice in common; bring the Nāsatyas hither for friendship.
O Indra, you caused the waters to flow; O Hero, the Aśvins bestowed thousands of gifts.
Rejoicing according to the Truth for the sake of progeny, Indra, with his vigorous friends, pursued his purpose.
For by means of these wondrous powers he approached the Dasyu; he scattered the mists and cast down the darkness.

RV 10.73.6: Even those of the same name you struck down; Indra, you blew them away as the Dawn [blows away] darkness. With your lofty, eager friends you went forth; together you struck down their heart-felt foundations. RV 10.73.7: You struck down Namuci, who was eager for the sacrifice, making the Dāsa lose his magical power (*vimāya*), just as you did for the seers. You made pleasant paths for Manu, leading toward the gods, like easy ways to travel.
You have filled these names; O Indra, as the Lord, you hold them in your hand.
The gods rejoice in your power; you have turned the trees upside down.
When his wheel was set down in the waters, even then he found the honey for him.

That udder which is fixed upon the earth, the milk which you placed within the cows and the plants— When they say, "He has gone forth as a horse," I consider him to be born of vital power (*ojas*). He has gone forth from wrath and has taken his stand in the dwellings; Indra alone knows whence he was born.
Like strong-winged birds, the Priyamedha seers have approached Indra with their supplications. Dispel the darkness, fill our eyes with light, and release us like those bound in a snare.
Whether through the praise of the Vasus, or through prayer, or through sacrifices, I desire to worship you, O Lord of the two worlds.
RV 10.74.1: Those who are like swift steeds when it comes to winning wealth, or who, being renowned, have bestowed fame upon the worshiper— RV 10.74.2:
At their invocation, the Asura reached toward heaven; with a mind seeking glory, the craftsman fashioned [the hymn].
Where the gods, looking on for the sake of well-being, act as if with their own desirable gifts, like the sky.
This is the song of these immortals who yearn for treasure in its full perfection;
may they, who perfect both our prayer and the sacrifice, bestow upon us complete wealth.
O Indra, those seekers of you praise that [deed] of yours, they who have broken open the stall rich in cattle.
RV 10.74.4: Those who, at once, desired to milk the great, vast earth—mother of many sons—with her thousand streams;

RV 10.74.5: O powerful ones, bring Indra here for our protection—he who is unsubdued, who subdues those who attack us, the lord of the *Ṛbhus*, the bounteous one worthy of beautiful praise, who, rich in food, bears the thunderbolt for the sake of men.
Whatever he has accomplished most abundantly in the past, the Vṛtra-slayer Indra has filled himself with his names.
The mighty lord of power has become manifest; whatever we desire him to do, may he perform that.
O Waters, the poet shall proclaim your supreme greatness in the dwelling of Vivasvat.
The seven times seven have indeed moved forth in three ways; the Sindhu has surged forward with might over the flowing streams.
Varuṇa carved out paths for you to travel, O Sindhu, when you rushed toward the prizes.
From the high ground you flow along the slope and over the ridges, as you rule over the foremost of these moving things.
In heaven his roar extends above the earth; he raises up infinite vigor with his light.
Like rains from a cloud, the showers thunder forth when the Sindhu goes roaring like a bull.
Toward you, O Sindhu, the rivers rush like lowing mothers toward their young, like milch-cows toward their milk.
Like a warrior king, you lead them forward; when you reach their head, you descend along the steep slope.
O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Śutudrī, Paruṣṇī—follow this my prayer!
O Marudvṛdhā, with the Asiknī, Vitastā, and Ārjīkīyā, and with the Suṣoma, hear my call!
First, with the Tṛṣṭāmā, she hastens to flow; united with the Sasartu and the Rasā, and with the Aśvī, O Sindhu.
With the Kubhā, the Gomatī, the Krumu, and the Mehatnu, you travel on a single chariot—those [rivers] by which you go forth.
Straight-moving, bright, and radiant in her greatness, she carries across the expanses and the regions.
The Sindhu is unassailable, the most active among the waters, beautiful to behold like two brilliant mares of wondrous form.
The Sindhu possesses fine horses, fine chariots, and fair garments; she is golden, well-fashioned, rich in swift steeds.
The youthful maiden is wool-soft and adorned with silk; clothed in these, the blessed one increases the sweetness [of our lives].
He has yoked his easy-gliding chariot drawn by swift horses; with it, may he win the prize in this contest.
For great indeed is his majesty praised—the unassailable, self-glorious, and overflowing one.
I urge you toward us at the dawning of strength; O Maruts, Indra, and the two worlds, anoint him.
So that both day and night may be our companions, may they grant us wide space at every seat of sacrifice, O breakers-forth.
Therefore, press out this most excellent libation;
like a stone held in the hands, let it flow for the presser.
For the noble one has bestowed upon us preeminent manly power for great wealth, as he directed his mind toward the swift steed.
This very libation of his has brought forth the waters, just as in the past it brought the path to Manu.
In the sacrifice of Tvaṣṭṛ’s son, who was surrounded by a flood of cattle and adorned with horses, they have established the sacrificial rites within the rituals.
Strike away the treacherous Rākṣasas; hold back Nirṛti and drive away ill-will.
Press out for us wealth consisting of all heroic sons; O stones, bring forth the hymn that reaches the gods.
Even from heaven, [I call] to you who are more powerful, and with Vibhvan, to those who are swifter in deed.
To those who are more eager for the *soma* than even Vāyu, and who perform better service for the father than even Agni—to them [be praise].
May our glorious pressing-stones (*grāvāṇaḥ*) resound with their heavenly, celestial voice as they press out the exhilarating juice.
Where the men milk the desirable honey, shouting aloud on all sides, vying with one another.
The chariot-borne stones press out the Soma; seeking the kine, they milk forth its juice.
They milk the udder for the purpose of pouring it out; the men purify the offering with their mouths.
O stones, you have become skillful men, you who press the Soma for Indra.
The most desirable thing for you, for your divine abode; the most excellent wealth for you, for the earthly one who presses the juice.
Like those who sprinkle from the clouds, I sprinkle wealth with my voice; like those possessing oblations, we know the sacrifice.
I shall praise this host of the Maruts, worthy of prayer, so that it may be glorious for them.
For the sake of glory, the youths have prepared their ornaments through many nights, like those of the good Maruts.
The sons of Dyaus have come forth like goats; these Ādityas have grown strong.
They who by their own power have surpassed heaven and earth, as the sun surpasses the clouds.
