Like two plowmen, sweating with exertion, you two attend to the field with vigor as if from a well-watered pasture.
May we prosper in our hymn of praise, may we win the prize; come here to our prayer, O you who ride in one chariot!
Like ripened honey within the cows, the Aśvins have fulfilled the desire for the portion of beings. Their great bounty has become manifest; every living thing has been released from darkness.
The great light given by the Fathers has arrived; the broad path of the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) has appeared.
High in heaven abide those who give sacrificial fees; those who give horses dwell together with the sun.
Those who give gold partake in immortality; O Soma, those who give clothing prolong their lives.
Divine is the fulfillment, the sacrificial fee, and the worship of the gods; for they do not give to the stingy.
Then, O men, with outstretched sacrificial fees, many offer gifts out of fear of reproach.
They behold the oblation—Vāyu who flows in a hundred streams, the Sun that finds the light, and the one who watches over men.
Those who give and bestow at the assembly milk the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) whose mother is sevenfold.
The giver of sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*) comes first when summoned; the giver of sacrificial fees goes at the head as the leader of the village.
Him alone I consider the lord of men who was the first to bestow a sacrificial fee.
Him indeed they call a seer (*ṛṣi*), him a priest (*brahmán*), the director of the sacrifice, the chanter of Sāmans, and the reciter of hymns (*uktha*).

He knows the three bodies of the bright one, he who was the first to succeed through the sacrificial gift (*dakṣiṇā*). The sacrificial gift bestows the horse; the sacrificial gift bestows the cow; the sacrificial gift bestows the glittering gold.
The sacrificial gift wins food for him who gives it as his own self; the wise man makes the sacrificial gift his armor.
The liberal patrons do not die; they do not go to ruin; they are not harmed, nor do they tremble—the liberal patrons.
This entire world, both this earth and the heavens, he gives all of it as sacrificial fees to them.
The liberal patrons have first won a fragrant dwelling; the liberal patrons have won a bride beautifully attired.
The liberal patrons have won the right to drink the soma within; the liberal patrons have won, they who go forth even when uninvited.
For the liberal patron they groom the swift horse; for the liberal patron these maidens adorn themselves.
This dwelling of the liberal patron is like a lotus-pool, like a divine mansion, beautifully decorated and brilliant.
The well-bred horses carry the liberal patron; the swift chariot rolls along for the sake of the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*).
O gods, protect the liberal patron in battles; the liberal patron is the conqueror of enemies in the encounters.
Seeking what has Saramā come here? For the road is far, wearying, and leads away.
What was our summons? What was the night’s end? How did you cross the waters of the Rasā?
I travel as Indra’s envoy, sent forth, seeking your great treasures, O Paṇis. The leap across [the mountain] protected us out of fear; thus did I cross the waters of the Rasā.
RV 10.108.3: What sort of man is Indra, O Saramā, what is his appearance, he whose messenger you have come from afar to be?
RV 10.108.4: Let him come here; let us establish him as our friend, and then may he become the lord of our cattle.
RV 10.108.5: I do not know him to be one who can be deceived; rather, he is the deceiver of whomever I, as his messenger, have come from afar.
RV 10.108.4: Deep-flowing rivers do not hide him; slain by Indra, O Paṇis, you shall lie low.
RV 10.108.5: These are the cows, O Saramā, which you sought as you flew about the ends of heaven, O fortunate one. Who will release them to you without a fight? For our weapons are sharp.
O Paṇis, let your words be beyond the reach of an army; let your wicked bodies be incapable of being pierced by arrows.
Let the path you must travel be unassailable; may Bṛhaspati show mercy to both of us.
This treasure, O Saramā, lies at the base of the mountain, brimming with cattle, horses, and riches.
The Paṇis guard him who is well-guarded; they have gone to a deceptive, empty place.
May the Ṛṣis come here—those sharpened by Soma, the Ayāsyas, the Aṅgirases, and the Navagvas. They shall divide this stall of cattle among themselves, and then the Paṇis will regret these words.
Thus you have come, O Saramā, driven by divine force.
I shall make you my sister; do not go back. O fortunate one, we shall grant you a share of the cattle.
I know nothing of brotherhood nor of sisterhood; Indra and the terrible Aṅgirases know them.

RV 10.108.10: They seemed to me to desire cattle when this [sun] had stepped out from here; the Paṇis were far away. RV 10.108.11: Far away indeed are the Paṇis; let the cows come forth, breaking through by means of *ṛta*.
Bṛhaspati, Soma, the pressing-stones, and the inspired sages found those that were hidden.
They spoke first regarding the sin against the *brahman*: the boundless ocean, Mātariśvan, Vīḷuhara, the fierce Tapas, the bliss-bringing one, and the divine Waters, the first-born by *ṛta*.
King Soma was the first to return the wife of the *brahman*, not being made angry.

Varuṇa and Mitra followed after her; Agni, the Hotṛ-priest, led her away by the hand. "She must be taken by the hand alone; she is the wife of a Brahmin," so they said. She did not submit to a messenger sent to fetch her; thus is the kingdom protected by a Kṣatriya.
The gods and the seven seers who sat down for austerity spoke concerning her in the past.

A terrible wife, when led away from a Brahmin, brings instability even in the highest heaven. The student of sacred knowledge (*brahmacārī*) moves about performing his various duties; he becomes a single limb of the gods.
Through him, Bṛhaspati recovered his wife, who had been led away by Soma, as the gods [recovered] the *juhū* ladle. The gods gave her back; so too did men.
The kings, making their word true, gave back the Brahmin’s wife.
Having restored the wife of the Brahmin and been freed from sin by the gods,
they partake of the nourishment of the earth and worship the Wide-Striding One (Viṣṇu).
Kindled today in the house of man, O Jātavedas, you, a god, sacrifice to the gods.
And bring [the gods] hither, O thou of friendly luster, for thou art the wise messenger, the seer, and the perceptive one.
O Tanūnapāt, sweetening with honey the paths that lead along the way of Truth, do thou, O fair-tongued one, make them savory.
Fulfilling our thoughts through our prayers and our sacrifice, perform our rite among the gods.
Being invoked, worthy of praise, and worthy of adoration, come, O Agni, in harmony with the Vasus!
You are the youthful Hotṛ-priest of the gods; as such, being impelled, sacrifice to them as the most skilled sacrificer.
The sacred grass is strewn eastward according to the direction of the earth; it is spread at the beginning of the days for her who provides the dwelling.
It spreads out further and wider, a spacious womb for the gods and for Aditi.
Let the wide-opening doors swing open far apart, like wives adorning themselves for their husbands. O divine, lofty, all-impelling doors, be easy of access for the gods.
Pressing the juice, the two worshipful ones, Dawn and Night, sit down close together in their common dwelling-place—
the two celestial maidens, lofty and adorned with golden ornaments, assuming a radiant splendor of brilliant hues.
The two divine Hotṛ-priests, the first, eloquent ones, measuring out the sacrifice so that man may worship.
Impelling [the sacrifice] at the assemblies, the two poets who point out the eastern light with their direction—
may Bhāratī come quickly to our sacrifice, and Iḷā, making us mindful here as among men. May the three goddesses, Sarasvatī and the skillful ones, sit upon this pleasant sacrificial grass.
He who has fashioned these two parents, Heaven and Earth, and all existing worlds with their various forms—

him, the god Tvaṣṭṛ, do thou, the most skilled sacrificer, being wise and impelled by the Hotṛ, worship here today. Anointing them, release the oblations in due season for the path of the gods, according to thy own nature.
May the Lord of the Forest, the divine Agni the immolator, season the oblation with honey and clarified butter.
As soon as he was born, Agni measured out the sacrifice; he became the leader of the gods.
At the command of this Hotṛ, in the speech of Truth (Ṛta), may the gods eat the oblation consecrated with Svāhā.
O wise ones, bring forth your inspired hymn, according as the thoughts of men arise.
Let us impel Indra with truthful deeds, for he is the hero who loves songs of praise and is well-known.
For the thought from the seat of Truth has shone forth; the bull, the son of the herd, has come together with the cows.
He rose up with a mighty roar; he has pervaded even the vast intermediate spaces.

Indra indeed knows this by report, for he is the victorious one who prepares the path for Sūrya. Making the cow his consort, the unshakable one became the lord of heaven; born of old, he is irresistible.
Indra, praised by the Aṅgirases, has with his greatness shattered the laws of the mighty ocean;
he has spread out many regions and, as a warrior, supported the firmament through his truthfulness.
Indra is the counterpart of heaven and earth; he knows all libations and slays Śuṣṇa.
He extended even the vast heaven with the sun; he, the most steadfast, propped it up with a pillar as a support.
For with his thunderbolt, the slayer of Vṛtra struck down Vṛtra and the illusions of the swelling god.
O bold one, you have boldly struck him down here; thus, O Maghavan, you became mighty-armed in strength.
The Dawns have come together with Sūrya; his rays have found the wondrous light.
When that star of heaven first became visible, no one truly knows from where it returns. Far indeed have those waters gone, the first of them which flowed forth at Indra’s impulse.

RV 10.111.8: Where indeed is their summit? Where is their base? And where now is your middle? RV 10.111.9: You released the rivers that had been swallowed by the dragon; then, with speed, they surged forth.
Those seeking release and those already released—now these, sharpened as they were, flow down without ceasing.
Moving together like longing women toward the river, the ancient lover has come, the breaker of their forts. O Indra, may your earthly treasures and many blessings reach us;
may your favors come to us. O Indra, drink of the pressed juice according to your desire, for the morning libation is your first draught.
Rejoice, O Hero, to slay the enemies; we shall proclaim your heroic deeds with hymns of praise.
O Indra, come on that chariot of yours which is swifter than thought, for the drinking of the Soma.
Let your bay horses hasten quickly, those stallions with whom you come, rejoicing.
With the golden-hued splendor of the sun, make thy body radiant with the most excellent forms.
O Indra, being invoked by us, thy friends, sit down and rejoice together with us.
Thy greatness, in whose exhilaration these two great worlds, heaven and earth, could not contain—that very greatness is thine.
Come, O Indra, with your beloved, harnessed bay horses to that dwelling, toward the dear food.
O Indra, having drunk of that [Soma] repeatedly, you have made your enemies subject to your will and worthy of battle.
That [Soma] stirs for you abundance and power; that Soma has been pressed for your exhilaration, O Indra.
RV 10.112.6: O Indra, Lord of a hundred powers, drink this Soma from this cup of yours, which is well-provided with wealth;
it is a full vessel of intoxicating sweetness, which all the gods indeed desire. RV 10.112.7:
For from many sides, O Indra, men who have set forth their offerings call upon you, the Bull.
May these most honey-sweet libations of ours be yours; O Indra, take pleasure in them! I shall proclaim, O Indra, your ancient deeds and those heroic exploits first performed.
In your true wrath you loosened the mountain; you made the cow easy to find for the one who offers prayer.
Sit down among the hosts, O Lord of Hosts; they call you the wisest of poets among the seers.
Nothing whatsoever is done without you in the distance; O Maghavan, great and wondrous one, sing your praise!
Look upon us who implore you, O Maghavan; O Friend, be mindful of your friends, O Lord of Wealth.
Grant us joy, O maker of joy, you of true vigor; grant us our share even in wealth that has not yet been apportioned.
May Heaven and Earth, being of one mind with all the gods, protect his vigorous power.
When he came, performing his greatness and Indra-power, having drunk of the Soma, he increased according to his will.
Viṣṇu, having discharged his arrow with might, proclaims this greatness of his as he flows with honey.
Having slain Vṛtra together with the gods who accompany him, Indra, the bounteous one, became preeminent.
When you stood firm for battle, bearing weapons against the serpent Vṛtra, you obtained the prize of victory.
RV 10.113.3: Here, O fierce one, all the Maruts together with their own selves increased your majesty and your Indra-power.
RV 10.113.4: As soon as he was born, he drove away his rivals; the hero looked upon manly deeds and the field of battle.
He split the mountain, released the flowing waters, and by his skillful work, he propped up the wide firmament.
Then Indra truly assumed his powers; he pressed heaven and earth further apart.
Boldly he hurled down the iron thunderbolt, a blessing for Mitra, Varuṇa, and the donor.
Here, before the powers of the swelling Indra, they fled from the wrath of the impetuous one.
When the fierce one, bearing the waters enveloped by darkness, cut Vṛtra asunder with his might;

when the two [powers] strove together, contending with their greatness for the first heroic deeds to be performed— Indra, struck down by his own power at the first invocation, cast off the thick darkness.
Then all the gods, through their desire for eloquence inspired by Soma, magnified your manly powers.
Vṛtra was subdued by Indra’s blow; like Agni with his jaws, he consumed the parched food.
Proclaim aloud, with many skillful words and hymns, your friendships with him through your bonds of friendship.
Indra, subduing both Dhuni and Cumuri, heeded Dabhīti because of his faithful devotion.
Bring us many excellent horses, by which I may think upon and praise your words of counsel.
May we cross all difficulties by easy paths; find for us today a wide and deep ford.
The two heats have pervaded the threefold world on all sides; Mātariśvan has come to their delight.
Desiring to obtain the milk of heaven, they have sought it; the gods know the hymn of power.
Three messengers wait upon Nirṛti for her command; the far-famed bearers of the oblation discern them clearly.

The seers have discerned their foundation in the highest, secret ordinances. The young woman with four braided locks, beautifully adorned, wearing ghee upon her face, clothes herself in sacred wisdoms.
Upon her two strong-winged bulls have settled, where the gods have established their portion.
The single, fair-winged bird has entered the ocean; he gazes upon this entire world.
With a simple mind, I beheld him nearby; his mother licks him, and he licks his mother.
The wise poets, with their words, fashion the one fair-winged bird into many forms.
Establishing the meters at the sacrifices, they measure out twelve cups of Soma;
fashioning the thirty-six and the four, they establish the meters up to twelve. Having measured out the sacrifice with inspired thought, the sages set the chariot in motion with the *Ṛg* and *Sāman*.
His other glories are fourteen; the seven sages lead them forth with their speech.
Who here can declare the ford that reaches [the goal], the path by which they drink of the pressed juice? Fifteenfold are the hymns in a thousand ways; as vast as heaven and earth, so great is that.
A thousandfold are its greatnesses; a thousandfold is the extent to which Brahman is spread out—so great is Speech.
What wise man knows the union of the meters? Who has attained the responsive voice of the *dhiṣṇya* priests?
Whom do they call the eighth hero among the officiants? And who indeed has discerned the two bay steeds of Indra?
Some wander around the edge of the earth; they have stood yoked to the poles of the chariot.
When Yama has been established in his dwelling, they distribute the reward for their labor among these [beings].
Wondrous indeed is the growth of the young infant, who does not go to his two mothers in order to suckle.

If she who has no udder gave birth and he, though small, grew great instantly, performing his great mission as a messenger—Agni, indeed, was established by name as the most skillful in his work, he who gathers the forests together with his tooth of ash.
With his tongue that crushes all, he is the master of the well-performed sacrifice; like a bull snorting in the pasture, he is impetuous.
Like a falcon perched upon a tree, that god—Indu, who snorts and scatters the flood, the ocean;
like a carrier with his mouth, roaring with flame, you of mighty vows, who traverse the paths.
O ageless one, as you spread abroad, the unshakable winds do not encompass you, even as you burn.

Like joyful warriors, they have reached the hero Trita, urging him on toward his desired goal. This Agni is most like a Kaṇva; he is the friend of Kaṇva, the overcomer of the enemy, whether far or near.
May Agni protect those who praise him; may Agni protect the patrons; may Agni grant us their protection.
RV_10.115.06.1 {19} To Jātavedas, the most powerful victor, the son of the fathers, [I pray] as he hastens eagerly along.
RV_10.115.06.2 {19} He who, with boldness, grants a boon even in the waterless desert to one seeking it, to that greatest of the great who desires to give in the wilderness.
RV_10.115.07.1 {19} Thus Agni, the Son of Strength, is praised for wealth by mortals together with patrons and by men.
Like well-disposed friends, they who follow the *ṛta* surpass men in splendor like the heavens.
"O Son of Strength, O Victorious One!"—thus does the bull-like voice of Upastuta praise you.
We shall praise you; through you may we have heroic sons, extending our lifespan even further.
Thus, O Agni, have the seers, the Upastutas, the sons of Vṛṣṭihavya, spoken to you.
Protect them—the singers and the patrons. "Vaṣaṭ! Vaṣaṭ!"—thus they have reached upward; "Homage! Homage!"—thus they have reached upward.
Drink the Soma for great Indra-power; drink it, most excellent one, for the slaying of Vṛtra.
Drink for wealth and for strength, being invoked; drink the honeyed mead, O Indra, and be strong.
Drink of this nourishing Soma that has been set forth, O Indra, of the best pressed juice.
As a giver of well-being, rejoice in your mind; turn toward us for the sake of abundant fortune.

May the divine Soma exhilarate you, O Indra; may he who is pressed among the earthly peoples exhilarate you. May he by whom you have created wide space exhilarate you; may he by whom you drive away your enemies exhilarate you.
Let the doubly-powerful, unassailable Indra, the bull, come with his two bay steeds to the poured-out food.
For the sake of cattle, drink of the pressed, offered honey-sweet soma; utterly overcome the weariness of the foe, O Bull.
Causing the sharp weapons of the impetuous to blaze forth, strike down the firm defenses of those who hasten in their attack.
To you, the fierce one, I grant power and strength; having encountered the enemies, rend them in their battles.
O Indra, extend your fame; ward off our adversaries with strength, as one wards off enemies with a firm bow.
Increasing toward us with your powers, O unassailable one, cause your body to grow strong.
O Maghavan, this oblation is offered to you; O Sovereign, accept it without anger.
For you, O Maghavan, is the pressed juice; for you is the cooked offering. Eat, O Indra, and drink of that which has been set forth.
Eat indeed, O Indra, these presented oblations; take pleasure in the cooked food and the Soma. Bearing offerings, we welcome you; may the desires of the sacrificer come true.
RV_10.116.09.1 With a desire for eloquent speech, I send forth [this hymn] to Indra and Agni; with my songs of praise, I urge them on as one drives a boat upon the river.
RV_10.116.09.2 Like spokes of a wheel, the gods revolve around us—those who are the givers of wealth and the breakers-through [of obstacles].
RV_10.117.01.1 Truly, O gods, hunger is not a weapon that you have bestowed; even when one has eaten, deaths come upon him.
Moreover, the wealth of the one who gives does not diminish; indeed, the one who does not give finds no comforter.

He who, though possessing food, hardens his heart against the needy man who comes to him in longing for nourishment—having previously served him, he now finds no comforter. He who makes his mind firm [in refusal] finds no one to soothe him.
He alone is a liberal giver who bestows upon the needy who wanders about, emaciated and seeking food.
He is ready for him when summoned on the journey; moreover, he makes him his friend in future times.
He is no friend who does not give to a friend who stays with him, who comes to him seeking sustenance.
Let him depart from this man; that dwelling is not his. He would rather seek another who gives, even one who is a stranger.
The more powerful man should give to the suppliant; he should look toward a path that is far more extended.
For riches revolve like the wheels of a chariot; they attend upon one after another.
The thoughtless man gains food in vain; I speak the truth: it is his own destruction. He nourishes neither the noble lord nor his friend; he who eats alone becomes the possessor of sin alone.
Indeed, the ploughshare that tills the earth provides nourishment; by its movements, it clears the path for the traveler.
Speaking, the Brahmin is more worthy than the one who does not speak; the liberal kinsman shall prevail over the one who is not liberal.
The one-footed has stepped beyond the two-footed; the two-footed overtakes the three-footed from behind.
The four-footed comes to the call of the two-footed, looking upon the fivefold rows as he stands near.
Even two hands that are alike do not perform the same work; even two mother-cows do not yield the same amount of milk.
Even twins do not possess equal strength; even two who are kinsmen do not give gifts in equal measure.
O Agni, shining among mortals, you strike down the devouring demon.
O you of pure vows, in your own dwelling,
you rise up when well-invoked; you take delight in the offerings of clarified butter when the ladles have been raised toward you.
Offered with oblation, Agni shines forth, he who is to be praised with song;
his face is anointed with the ladle. Agni is anointed with clarified butter, he whose face is honey-sweet when offered with oblation.
Shining, rich in light,
being praised, you are kindled as the bearer of oblations for the gods;
as such, mortals invoke you.
O mortals, worship that immortal Agni with clarified butter—
the inviolable lord of the household. O Agni, burn away the demon with your inviolable flame.
Shine as the guardian of the cosmic order (ṛta).
O Agni, with your face, burn against the sorceresses,
shining brightly among the wide dwellings.
Thee, O carrier of oblations, dwelling in wide space, they have kindled with hymns,
thee the most excellent sacrificer among the human race.
"Thus," so says my mind, "may I win cattle and horses."
"Will they perhaps drink of the Soma? "Like violent winds, the draughts have lifted me up. "Will they perhaps..."
The Soma juices drunk have lifted me up, like swift horses drawing a chariot.
The prayer has approached me, like a lowing cow toward her dear calf.
RV_10.119.04.2: Will [he come]? RV_10.119.05.1: Like a carpenter fashioning a chariot-seat, I turn my thought around within my heart.
RV_10.119.05.2: Will [he come]?
The five tribes have not even glances cast upon me;
will they not [come to me]? Neither both worlds, heaven and earth, equal my other wing.
By my greatness I have surpassed the sky and this great earth.
Come now, I shall set this earth down here or there; would it not be so?
Swiftly indeed shall I strike the earth here or there.
RV_10.119.10.2 {27} Will it be so?
... RV_10.119.11.1 {27} One wing of mine is in heaven; the other I have drawn down below. RV_10.119.11.2 {27} Will it be so? ...
I am the one of great majesty, risen up toward the vault of heaven.
Will [he not grant]...? I go quickly to the dwelling, the bearer of oblations for the gods, well-prepared.
RV_10.119.13.2{27} Will it not be so?
RV_10.120.01.1{01} That indeed was the eldest in all worlds, from which was born the fierce one, whose valor is brilliant.
RV_10.120.01.2{01} As soon as he is born, he overcomes his enemies—he whom all the helpers rejoice in.

Increasing in strength and possessing abundant power, he, as an enemy, strikes fear into the Dāsa. Winning both the unbreathing and the breathing, they cry out to you when the offerings are presented at the feasts. All turn their will toward you, since these helpers become twofold or even threefold.
Mix the sweet with what is sweeter than sweet; fight well for us with honey against the honeyed foe.
For thus indeed, O Bold One, do the sages rejoice after you in every intoxication as you win the riches.
Extend your more powerful and firm strength; let not the evil-doing sorcerers harm you.
Through you we prevail in battles, beholding many things worthy of combat. I urge on your weapons with my words; I sharpen your vital powers with my prayer.
I would praise the one of many forms, the skillful, the most unassailable, the Aptya among the Aptyas.
He displays his power against the seven Dānus; he overcomes many adversaries.
You bestow that which is near and that which is far, in the house wherein you have protected us with your aid.
You cause the two wandering Mothers to stand firm; from there, you impel many heroic deeds.
These prayers, which win the light of heaven, does Bṛhaddiva, the foremost winner of the sun, proclaim as strength for Indra.
He rules over the great stall of cattle as self-sovereign; he has thrown open all his own doors.
Thus has the great Bṛhaddiva Atharvan spoken: his own body is none other than Indra.
The sisters dwelling in the mother, stainless, impel him with power and cause him to grow.
In the beginning, the Golden Embryo (Hiraṇyagarbha) came into being; once born, he was the sole Lord of all that exists.
He supported this earth and yonder sky. To what god shall we offer our oblation?
He who is the giver of self, the giver of strength, whose command all the gods revere;
he whose shadow is immortality and whose [other side] is death—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
He who by his greatness became the sole king of the breathing and blinking world.
He who rules over these bipeds and quadrupeds—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
He whose greatness these snow-capped mountains proclaim, whose they say is the ocean along with the Rasā river;
he to whom these quarters belong, whose they are, whose are his two arms—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?

By whom the fierce heaven and the earth were made firm, by whom the sky was propped up and the vault of heaven established; he who is the measurer of the mid-region within the realm of space—to what god shall we offer our oblation?
He toward whom the two shouting armies, supported by his aid, looked up with trembling minds as they shook.
RV 10.121.6: Wherein the risen sun shines forth—unto which god shall we offer worship with our oblation?

RV 10.121.7: When the great waters went everywhere, bearing the germ and generating Agni, from that there arose the one life-force (*asus*) of the gods—unto which god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
He who by his greatness surveyed the waters as they held skill (*dakṣa*) and brought forth sacrifice;
he who was the one God above the gods—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
May he not harm us, he who is the progenitor of the earth, or he who, whose laws are truth, generated heaven.
And he who brought forth the great, shining waters—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
O Prajāpati, none other than you has encompassed all these created beings.
Whatever desire we have as we sacrifice to you, may that be ours; may we be masters of riches.

I praise him who is like a treasure, of wondrous luster—the lovely, gracious guest who is not to be hated. May he, Agni, the Hotṛ-priest and lord of the household, grant us all-sustaining riches and heroic strength.
O Agni, you of goodly wisdom, knowing all ways, graciously accept and delight in my word.
Anointed with clarified butter, impel the path for the sacred word; the gods have brought you forth according to your law.
As an immortal, moving around the seven stations, grant gifts to the donor who has performed good deeds.
O Agni, be pleased with him who has reached you with fuel, and grant him wealth consisting of heroic sons and self-sustaining prosperity.
Those possessing oblations invoke him, the banner of sacrifice, the first domestic priest, the one with seven steeds.
They call upon Agni, who hears us, whose back is anointed with ghee, the god who bestows heroic vigor upon the giver.
You are the first messenger, most excellent; being invoked, do you partake of the immortal draught.
The Maruts purified you in the house of the donor; the Bhṛgus caused you to shine forth with their hymns of praise.

O Agni of noble will, milking for the sacrifice-loving patron nourishment that is easy to milk and all-sustaining, you, dripping with ghee and illuminating the three cosmic orders, display your skill as you go around the sacrificial path.
At the break of this dawn, men have made you their messenger and have sacrificed to you.
The gods have strengthened you for your great majesty, O Agni, as they purified your sovereignty at the sacrifice.
The Vasiṣṭhas, the wise ones, chanting your praises, have invoked you, the powerful one, O Agni, at the assemblies.
Bestow upon the sacrificers an abundance of wealth; do you all protect us always with your blessings.
This Vena, the offspring of Pṛśni, has impelled the light-enveloped [rays] across the expanse of the mid-world.
At the meeting-place of the waters and the sun, the inspired singers lick him like a young child with their hymns.
Vena, born from the ocean, raises up the wave; the back of the beloved one has been seen.
Upon the ridge, on the summit of *Ṛta*, he shines as a brother; the hosts have lowed toward their common birthplace.
Many mothers of the calf, lowing together, stand there, dwelling in the same nest.
Moving upon the ridge of Truth, the voices of the immortal honey strike down the enemies.
Knowing his form, the sages yearned; they followed the cry of the wild buffalo.
Going by Truth, they have mounted the river; the Gandharva has found the immortal names.
The Apsaras, smiling at her lover, the maiden, bears him in the highest heaven.
Moving among the wombs of his beloved, being beloved himself, that Seer (Vena) sits upon the golden wing.
When they, longing with their hearts, beheld thee—the fair-winged bird flying toward the firmament—then did they gaze upon thee.
The golden-winged messenger of Varuṇa, the restless bird in the womb of Yama;
The Gandharva has stood erect upon the vault of heaven, bearing his brilliant weapons toward us.
Clothed in a fragrant robe, fair to behold, he has generated his own dear names in the light.
When the drop goes toward the ocean, beholding with the eye of a vulture in the firmament;
when the ray, longing for them with bright luster, has made dear things in the third realm of space.
O Agni, come to this sacrifice of ours, which has five courses, threefold, and seven threads.
He is our bearer of oblations and our leader; for a long time indeed you have lain in deep darkness.
Moving from the godless to the god, going secretly while perceiving immortality, I go forth.
Since I, being auspicious, abandon the inauspicious, I depart from my own kinship to seek a new kinsman.

Beholding the guest of another branch, they have measured out the many foundations of the Cosmic Order (*ṛta*). I offer praise to the Father, the Asura, for his favor; from that which is unworthy of sacrifice, I go toward the portion worthy of sacrifice. I have spent many years within him; choosing Indra, I leave my father behind.

Agni, Soma, and Varuṇa—these depart; the kingdom has turned away. I am coming hither to that kingdom. Those Asuras have become devoid of magic power. And you, O Varuṇa, do not love me. Discerning the truth from untruth, O King, come to the sovereignty over my kingdom by means of the *ṛta*.
This is the light; this has become lovely; this is the manifestation, the wide mid-air.

Let us two slay Vṛtra; come forth, O Soma! Being the oblation, let us worship thee with the oblation. The Seer, by his seership, fixed his form in heaven; Varuṇa, through his power, released the waters.
Like women making their homes secure, the rivers bear his bright color; pure, they carry it hither and thither.
They attend to his supreme power; they dwell with him, rejoicing in their own inherent nature.
Like subjects choosing a king, they have turned away from Vṛtra, loathing him, and have stood apart.
They call him the swan, the companion of the loathsome ones, moving in friendship with the celestial waters.
The seers, through their inspired thought, have perceived Indra as he moves along the *anuṣṭubh* meter.
I move with the Rudras and the Vasus; I move with the Ādityas and all the Viśvedevas.
I support both Mitra and Varuṇa; I support Indra and Agni; I support both the Aśvins.
I support the bountiful Soma; I support Tvaṣṭṛ, as well as Pūṣan and Bhaga. I bestow wealth upon the one who offers oblations, the zealous sacrificer who presses the soma.
I am the sovereign ruler, the gatherer of treasures, the conscious one, the first among those worthy of sacrifice.
The gods have distributed me in many places, dwelling in many abodes and entering into many forms.
Through me alone does he eat food, who sees, who breathes, and who hears what is spoken.
Those who do not understand wait upon me; hear, O famous one, for I speak with faith to you.
I myself alone declare this, which is pleasing to both gods and men. Whomever I desire, him I make fierce; him I make a Brahman, him a seer, him a man of great wisdom.
I bend the bow for Rudra, so that his arrow may strike down the one who hates sacred prayer. I stir up strife among the people; I have entered heaven and earth.
Upon the head of this [universe] I bring forth the father; my source is within the waters, in the midst of the ocean.
From there I spread out through all the worlds; I touch even that sky with my highest reach.
I alone blow forth like the wind, setting all beings in motion; beyond the heavens and beyond this earth, I have come to be so great in majesty.
Neither distress nor misfortune, O gods, reaches that mortal— him Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuṇa, acting in harmony, lead safely beyond his enemies.
For we choose this very thing from you, O Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman.
By which [means] you protect the mortal from distress and lead him beyond his enemies—
may those very ones, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman, now come for our protection.
They are the best leaders to lead us, and the most effective deliverers to carry us across our enemies.
You protect the universe on every side—Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman.
In your dear protection may we abide, O excellent leaders, beyond our enemies.
O Ādityas—Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman—[lead us] past all failures.

We invoke the fierce Rudra with the Maruts, Indra, and Agni for our well-being, beyond the reach of our enemies. May Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman lead us safely across all difficulties, these kings of the people, beyond the reach of our enemies.
May Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman grant us prosperity for our protection;
may the Ādityas, when we implore them, extend wide shelter over us beyond our enemies.
Just as you, O Vasus, worthy of worship, released even the buffalo cow that was bound by the foot.
Thus, O Agni, release us from distress; further prolong our span of life.
Night, approaching as a goddess, has looked out in many places with her eyes;
she has clothed herself in all splendors.
The immortal goddess, filling the wide spaces,
drives away the darkness from the depths and the heights with her light; she has driven out her sister, Dawn, as she approaches.
May the darkness depart from here.
Come to us today, O Night, at whose approach we have settled down like birds in their dwelling upon a tree.

The villages have settled down; those with feet and those with wings have settled down, even the hawks seeking their prey have settled down. Drive away the she-wolf, drive away the wolf; O Night, drive away the thief.
And so, become easy for us to cross over.
The black darkness, clearly manifest, has approached me, thickly anointed. O Dawn, drive it away like a debt.
RV 10.127.8: O Night, daughter of Heaven, I have driven the cows toward you; choose my hymn of praise as one who has conquered.
RV 10.128.1: O Agni, may splendor be mine in our invocations; kindling you, may we nourish our own bodies.
May the four quarters bow down to me; with you as our overseer, may we conquer the enemy hosts.
May all the gods be on my side in this invocation—the Maruts led by Indra, Viṣṇu, and Agni.
May the vast expanse of the intermediate region be mine; may the wind blow for me in this desire of mine.
May the gods bestow wealth upon me through sacrifice; may the blessing be mine, and mine the invocation of the gods.
May the divine Hotṛ-priests, the foremost ones, accept my offerings; may we remain unharmed in body, possessing heroic sons.
Let them sacrifice for me with whatever oblations are mine; may the intention of my mind be fulfilled.
May I not fall into any sin whatsoever; O All-Gods, speak for us!
O six divine expanses, make wide room for us; O All-Gods, display your heroism here!
May we not be abandoned by our offspring nor by our bodies; may we not yield to the enemy, O King Soma!

O Agni, driving away the wrath of our enemies, you, the undeceivable guardian, protect us on every side. Let those who seek to harm us turn back; let the minds of these who wake against us be utterly destroyed.
The Ordainer of ordainers, he who is the Lord of the world, the divine savior who overcomes the malicious—[we call upon him].
May both Aśvins, Bṛhaspati, and the gods protect this sacrifice and the sacrificer from misfortune.
May the wide-striding, mighty bull, invoked by many and rich in food, grant us protection at this invocation.
O Indra, lord of bay horses, be gracious to our progeny; do not harm us, nor deliver us over to destruction.
RV 10.128.09.1: May those who are our rivals be driven away; with Indra and Agni, we repel them. RV 10.128.09.2:
The Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas have made me one who touches the highest, fierce, observant, and sovereign lord.
RV 10.129.01.1: Neither non-being nor being existed then; there was neither the atmospheric realm nor the sky beyond it.
What covered? Where? In whose protection? What was the water, deep and unfathomable?
Death did not exist, nor did immortality; there was no sign of night or day.
That One breathed, windless, by its own inherent power (*svadhā*); other than that, indeed, nothing else existed beyond it.
In the beginning there was darkness hidden by darkness; all this was an indistinguishable ocean.
That which was covered by the void, that One, was born through the power of heat. Desire arose in the beginning within it, which was the first seed of mind.
The wise, having pondered with their insight, discovered the kinship of the existent within the non-existent, having fixed it in the heart.
A transverse line was stretched across these; was there depth below it?
There were seed-bearers, there were powers; self-sustenance was below, and impulse was above.

Who truly knows? Who here can declare it—from where was it born, from where came this creation? The gods are later than its origin; so who then knows from where it first arose? Whether this creation was fashioned or whether it was not— Who knows that from which it arose?
Whether he who is in the highest heaven has indeed spread it out or not—He who surveys all things in the highest heaven, He alone knows, or perhaps even He does not know.
He who is its overseer in the highest heaven—he indeed knows it, or perhaps he does not know.

The sacrifice which is stretched out on all sides with threads, extended by a hundred and one divine acts—these fathers who have come weave it; they sit at the outspread [loom], saying, "Weave forward! Weave backward!"
The Man extends it and the Man cuts it out; the Man has stretched it across this firmament.
These pegs have settled near the seat; they have made the *sāman* chants as threads to weave through.
What was the measuring line? What the model? What was the foundation? What was the clarified butter? What was the enclosing-stick?
What was the meter, what the *prauga*, what the hymn (*uktha*), when all the gods sacrificed to the God?
The *gāyatrī* became the companion of Agni; Savitṛ was united with the *uṣṇih*.
Soma, great through his hymns, was joined with the *anuṣṭubh*; the *bṛhatī* protected the speech of Bṛhaspati.
The Virāj is the glory of Mitra and Varuṇa; the Triṣṭubh is Indra’s portion here of the day.
Through the Jagatī, he entered all the gods; by that, the seers and human beings were fashioned.
By that, the seers and human beings were fashioned; when the ancient sacrifice was born, our fathers [were formed].
Beholding them with my mind as if with an eye, I think of those ancients who performed this sacrifice.
The seven divine seers, accompanied by hymns (*stoma*), meters (*chandas*), and measures (*pramā*), returned according to their cycles.
Having gazed upon the path of the ancients, the wise ones took hold of it, just as charioteers seize the reins.

O Indra, O overcomer, drive away all enemies to the east, drive them away to the west, and drive them away to the north and to the south, so that we may rejoice in your wide protection. Verily, just as those who possess barley reap the grain in due order, separating it one after another; so do thou [drive away our foes].
Bring here, right here, the food of those who have not come to the trimming of the sacred grass (*barhis*) with their homage.
For there is no chariot-pole for you two to travel according to the seasons, nor has any glory been found by you in the gatherings.
Desiring cattle, seeking horses, and striving for strength, the inspired singers approach Indra, the bull, for friendship.

O Aśvins, lords of splendor, drinking the *surā* together with the Asura Namuci, you two aided Indra in his deeds. Like two parents aiding their son, O Aśvins, you both protected Indra with your poetic wisdom and wondrous powers.

When you drank the exhilarating Soma with your powers, O Maghavan, Sarasvatī refreshed you. May Indra, the good protector, the possessor of wealth, through his aids, be gracious; may he, the all-knowing, drive away hatred and grant us fearlessness. May we be masters of heroic vigor.
May we abide in the favor of that one worthy of sacrifice, and in his auspicious goodwill.
May that Indra, the good protector and possessor of wealth, drive our enemies far away from us.
The heaven, rich in praise, honors the sacrificer; the earth honors the sacrificer.
The two divine Aśvins increased the one who sacrificed with their favors.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, we worship you both, the sustainers of the people, who possess great bliss and are impelled by the truth.
Through your friendship and through our own deeds, may we overcome the Rākṣasas.
And now, when we desire to win from you that which is dear, seeking to obtain heritable wealth;
or when the giver prospers in his wealth, no one can restrain his riches. O Asura, that other [world] was born from heaven; you, O Varuṇa, are the king of all.
The head of the chariot has taken pleasure [in this]; one who harms the end-maker is not free from such sin.
In this bright one, purified by *śaka-pūta*, he strikes down the heroes who have gone against their friend when the sin has been committed.
When he bestows protection upon his own bodies—upon those dear and worthy of sacrifice—he shines forth.
For your mother is Aditi, O wise ones; like heaven and earth, she is purified with milk.
Bestow what is dear upon us; wash away the sun with your rays.
For you two have sat down as lords of the waters—[you who sit] upon the chariot, [you who sit] at the pole, [you who sit] upon the tree.
Nṛmedhas delivered us from distress when we were lamenting; Sumedhas delivered us from distress.
Sing forth this strengthening hymn for this Indra, whose chariot is foremost.
Even in the encounter, he is the maker of wide space, the slayer of Vṛtra in the clash of battles. Be our inspirer; let the bowstrings of our enemies snap upon their bows.
You released the rivers to flow downward;
you slew the serpent. O Indra, you were born without a rival; you nourish every desirable thing. Therefore, we embrace you; let the bowstrings of our enemies snap upon their bows.
May all hostilities be utterly dispersed; may the prayers of the noble man reach us.
O Indra, you are the hurler of the weapon of death at the enemy who seeks to slay us; let the bowstrings of those others snap upon their bows, for that bounty of yours bestows wealth.

O Indra, whatever person from around us directs his mind toward us with wolfish intent, cast him beneath our feet; you are the dispeller and the conqueror—let the bowstrings of those others snap upon their bows.

Whoever assails us, O Indra—whether he be a kinsman or a stranger—diminish his strength, as the great heaven [overshadows the earth]. May the bowstrings of our adversaries snap upon their bows. O Indra, we who long for you take hold of your friendship.
Lead us along the path of Truth past all difficulties;

let the bowstrings of our enemies snap upon their bows. O Indra, grant us that which yields a boon to the singer, so that the great cow with unbroken udders may swell for us with milk in a thousand streams.
Since you, O Indra, have filled both heaven and earth like the Dawn, you, the great sovereign of the mighty peoples, were begotten by the divine Mother; the auspicious Mother begot you.
Relax the firm strength of that mortal who acts with malice.
Cast him beneath our feet who seeks to harm us; the divine Mother gave birth [to you], the auspicious Mother gave birth [to you].
O slayer of enemies, O Śakra, with your powers and all your protections, O Indra, shake down those great, all-glittering refreshments; the divine Mother gave birth [to you]...
When you, O Śatakratu Indra, shake off all things like wealth for the one who presses the soma, along with your thousandfold aids— O Goddess, Mother...
let the lightning-flashes fall away on every side like drops of sweat.
RV_10.134.05.2: May ill-will depart from us like the fibers of dūrvā grass; may the divine mother... RV_10.134.06.1: For you, O wise one, bear a long hook as if it were a spear.
RV_10.134.06.2: With your former step, O Maghavan, strike down our offspring as if they were birds; may the divine mother...
O gods, we do not diminish you; we do not neglect you. We act in accordance with what is heard in the sacred mantras.
With our wings and our armpits, we clasp one another here.
Upon that tree with beautiful leaves where Yama drinks together with the gods—
RV 10.135.1: Here the Lord of the House, our father, looks back toward the ancients.
RV 10.135.2: Seeing him wandering there in that evil way, looking back toward the ancients, I looked upon him with envy; therefore, I longed for him again.
O boy, the new chariot without wheels which you fashioned with your mind—
which has a single horse, faces in every direction, and which you mount though no one sees it; the chariot which you, O boy, set in motion for the inspired singers (vipra).
The *sāman* followed him, like a boat placed upon the water.
Who gave birth to the youth? Who fashioned the chariot?
Who indeed might tell us today how it was that she became the one to be followed?
Just as she became the one who follows in death, so was the foremost part born from her;
from the foundation in front, the exit was made behind.
This is the seat of Yama, which is called the dwelling place of the gods.
This pipe of his is blown; this one is adorned with songs.
The long-haired one bears Agni; the long-haired one bears the poison; the long-haired one sustains the two worlds.
The long-haired one [is fit] for the sight of all the suns; the long-haired one is called this light.
The sages, girdled by the wind, wear soiled garments of reddish-brown;
they follow the blast of the wind when the gods have entered [into them].
Intoxicated by the state of a sage, we have stood firm amidst the winds.
O mortals, you behold only our bodies; [the bird] flies through the intermediate space, surveying all forms. The sage is the well-disposed friend of every god, for the sake of his good deeds.
The horse of Vāta, the friend of Vāyu, the sage impelled by the gods—
he dwells in both oceans, the eastern and the western.
Moving along the path of the Apsarases, the Gandharvas, and the wild beasts, he dwells there.
The long-haired one, the knower of the secret, the sweet and most intoxicating friend of Keśin—
Vāyu churned for him; indeed,
he pounded the Kunanna food with the cup of poison, when he drank together with Rudra.
O gods, you raise up again that which has been cast down; O gods, you restore again even him who has committed sin. These two winds blow from the ocean and from afar.
One [wind] blows toward you for skill; let the other blow away whatever is harmful.
O Wind, blow hither healing medicine; O Wind, blow away whatever is harmful.
For you, possessing all remedies, move as the messenger of the gods.
I have come to you with healing remedies and with means for safety. O skillful one, I have brought you blessing; I drive away your consumption.
May the gods protect you here; may the host of Maruts protect you.
May all beings protect [him], so that he may become free from disease. The waters indeed are healers; the waters drive away disease.
The waters are the healers of everything; may they provide a remedy for you.
With hands that have ten fingers, with a tongue that is the forerunner of speech—
with those two which bring no disease, we touch you. In your friendship, O Indra, those bearers, mindful of the *ṛta*, split Vala asunder.
Where, bestowing gifts, you released the waters for Kutsa at the dawning of the day, and performed wondrous deeds in the conflict;
You let loose the plants, you split the mountains, and you drove forth the kine; you drank the beloved honey.
You caused the trees to flourish by this wondrous power; the Sun shone forth through the hymn born of Truth.
Sūrya unyoked his chariot in the midst of heaven; the Ārya found the counterpart for the Dāsa.
Indra, acting with Ṛjiśvan, shattered the firm fortresses of the guileful Asura Pipru.
Boldly shattering those unassailable strongholds, he plundered the treasures of the godless ones and caused them to pay their debt.
Like the sun in the month, he has taken the wealth of the citadel; being praised, may he shatter the enemies with his radiant [weapon].
With an army that does not fight, the far-reaching slayer of Vṛtra, who cleaves asunder, bestows gifts; he sharpens his impetuous weapons.
He was terrified by Indra’s thunderbolt, the crusher; Śundhyu fled away, abandoning his wagon.
These are indeed your famous deeds, yours alone: that you made the one [day] into many days when there was no sacrifice.
You established the distribution of the months in the sky; by you, the Father bears the wheel-rim that has been split apart.
With sun-like rays and golden hair, Savitṛ has risen as an eternal light in the east.
At his impulse, Pūṣan goes forth, the wise guardian who beholds all beings. Beholding men, he sits in the midst of heaven, having filled the two worlds and the intermediate space.
He looks upon those that flow with ghee, extending from the eastern to the western sign.
The foundation of wealth, the gatherer of treasures, he beholds all forms with his powers;
like the god Savitṛ whose laws are true, he stands like Indra in the battle for riches.
O Soma, the waters, having seen the Gandharva Viśvāvasu, flowed forth according to the Eternal Order (ṛta).
Indra, hastening along, perceived that; he saw the enclosure of the sun from within these [waters]. May Viśvāvasu, the celestial Gandharva who measures the mid-air, sing this to us.
Whether it be what we know as truth or what we do not know, may he, impelling our thoughts, further our prayers.
He found the winner in the course of the rivers; he threw open the doors of the stone-fenced enclosures. Gandharva proclaimed their immortal waters; Indra understood the power of the dragons.
O Agni, yours is fame and vital strength; your rays shine mightily, O Lord of Light.
O thou of great luster, by thy might, O Sage, thou grantest praiseworthy strength to the donor.
With purifying brilliance, with radiant brilliance, with undiminished brilliance, thou risest up with thy light.
Moving between the two mothers as their son, thou art near; thou fillest both heaven and earth.
O Son of Strength, Jātavedas, rejoice in our excellent praises and our prayers, being well-disposed toward us.
In you they have gathered the sacrificial foods—those of many forms, with wondrous aids, born of noble lineage.
O Agni, ruling as lord, spread yourself abroad among living beings; bestow wealth upon us, O Immortal One!
You shine forth with a form that is beautiful to behold; you fulfill the effective will for gain.
To the wise one who ordains the sacrifice, who rules over great wealth— You bestow a fortunate gift of beauty, great nourishment, and effective riches.
Men have placed before them for their welfare Agni, the upholder of *ṛta*, the mighty one, visible to all.
O divine one, human generations praise you with song—you who have ears that hear, you who are most far-reaching.
O Agni, speak here to us; turn toward us with a gracious mind.
Bestow upon us, O Lord of the People; you are the giver of wealth to us.
May Aryaman bestow it upon us, may Bhaga, may Bṛhaspati, may the gods, and may Sūnṛtā, the goddess, grant us riches.
We invoke King Soma for protection, and Agni with our songs; we invoke the Ādityas, Viṣṇu, Sūrya, and Bṛhaspati the priest.
We invoke Indra, Vāyu, and Bṛhaspati, who are easy to call, here to this place.
So that all the people may be well-disposed toward us in our assembly,
urge Aryaman, Bṛhaspati, and Indra to grant gifts; [urge] Vāta, Viṣṇu, Sarasvatī, and the prize-winning Savitṛ.
O Agni, through your fires, increase our sacred word (*brahman*) and our sacrifice.
Do you impel us toward the assembly of the gods for the granting of wealth.
O Agni, son of strength, this singer has found refuge in you; for there is nothing else to which he may turn for protection.
For auspicious is your triple-layered protection; keep the weapons of those who wish us harm far away.
O Agni, your births proceed like a downward slope; like a companion, you subdue all beings.
May our coursers and our prayers win the prize; they go forward of their own accord like a herdsman.
Or indeed, O self-dependent Agni, you spare much brushwood as you devour it; even the fallow lands become mere deserts. Let us not provoke your fierce weapon and your might.
When you go devouring over the heights and down into the valleys, you move apart like an army eager for booty.
When the wind blows after your flame, you shave the earth as a barber shaves a beard.
His lines of chariots are visible; there is but one path, yet many are the chariots.
When, O Agni, you groom your arms, you seek the earth that lies spread out below.
Let your strength rise up, let your flame rise up, O Agni; let the spoils of the one who exerts himself rise up for you.
Gape wide, bow down, growing ever stronger; may all the Vasus sit upon you today.
This is the gathering place of the waters, the dwelling of the ocean.
Make for yourself another path from here; go along it according to your will.
Upon your way hither and your way away, let flowering durva grass grow;
let there be lakes and lotuses—these are the dwellings of the ocean.
Even that Atri, who was worn out by age, you made free for his journey like a horse,
when you, O Kakṣīvān, restored him like a new chariot.
And even that [Atri], whom the dustless ones strove to bring forth like a prize-winning steed.
Untie the firm knot, as you did for Atri, O youngest ones, from the mid-air! O heroes, most wondrous in deed, O radiant ones, strive to win over the prayers for Vatr̥ya;
for then, O heroes of heaven, our hymn of praise shall not be parted from you again.
O Aśvins, bestowers of great wealth, let that gift and your favor come to us;
O heroes, bring us across in the wide assembly to our dwelling place. You two rescued Bhujyu, who was tossing about in the ocean at the far end of the region.
Come hither with your winged steeds, O Nāsatyas, for the sake of our gain. With your favors, like two well-disposed physicians, come, O most bountiful ones, possessors of all wealth.
O Heroes, be present with us, like overflowing springs of nourishment.
For this immortal drop of yours, O [Indra], flows like a steed;
it is skillful, the all-sustaining nourisher for the wise one.
This poetic power, the *Ṛbhu*-like thunderbolt, is among us for the sake of the giver.
He bears aloft the golden ornament and the exhilarating drink, like the *Ṛbhu* who fashioned the effective draught.
Impetuous, a bull among his own kine, he has looked down upon the serpent-like waters for the sake of the falcon who performs his task.
That which the fair-winged one, the son of the falcon, brought from afar—
that which has a hundred wheels and whose path is hidden— that lovely, unassailable, ruddy measure of the soma-juice which the falcon brought for you with his foot.
By this [Soma], vitality is extended; by it, life is prolonged for living. By it, kinship is made to wake.
Thus indeed, O Indra, through the drop, you maintain great power even among the gods. By wisdom, O wise one, vitality is extended; by wisdom, this [Soma] is pressed from us.
I dig up this herb, this most powerful plant, by which one drives away the rival wife and by which one wins a husband. O you with upturned leaves, auspicious one, sent by the gods, victorious one!
Blow away my rival; make my husband mine alone. I am superior, I am superior; may I be superior to those who are superior. And let my rival be inferior, inferior even to those who are inferior.
I do not take her name; she finds no pleasure in this man.
We send the rival wife away indeed to the farthest distance. I am the conqueror, and you are the victorious one.
Having both become powerful, let us two overcome my rival wife.
I have placed this conquering power near you; I have invested you with greater might.
May your mind run after me like a cow toward her calf; may it run along its path like water toward a valley.
O Forest-Dweller, O Forest-Dweller, you who seem to vanish away—why do you not ask the way to the village? Why does fear not find you?
When the cicada chirps in response to the loud cry of the male frog, [the forest-dwellers hear you].
The forest goddess exults, as if being pursued by those who strike with clubs.
And she seems to eat like cattle; indeed, she appears like a dwelling house. Moreover, at evening, the forest goddess lets out her cries like carts.
"He calls for the cattle; he has felled the trees. Dwelling in the forest, at evening he thinks, "I have cried out.
The forest does not kill, unless another comes upon it.
Having eaten of the sweet fruit, he lies down at his pleasure.
I have praised the Forest, the mother of wild beasts, who is fragrant with the scent of ointment, sweet-smelling, and rich in food without the toil of cultivation.
I place my faith in your first wrath, when you slew Vṛtra and released the waters for the benefit of men.
When both heaven and earth tremble after you, even the earth itself shakes from your vigor, O wielder of the stone.
With your wondrous powers, O blameless one, you crushed the guileful Vṛtra with a mind seeking glory.
In the raids for cattle, men choose you; in all sacrifices where oblations are offered, they choose you.

O much-invoked one, take pleasure in these patrons who, O Maghavan, have increased as prosperers of wealth. They sing praises for the sake of offspring and descendants during times of distress, seeking the prize of wisdom and undaunted strength in the contest for wealth.
He indeed shall take pleasure in well-sustained wealth—he who understands his exhilarating, swift-moving power.
O Maghavan, strengthened by you and performing the sacrifice with offerings, he quickly wins booty and riches through his men.
O Maghavan, being praised, grant strength to our host; by your greatness, make wide room for us and bestow riches.
You are Mitra for us, a master of magic like Varuṇa; O wonder-worker, you distribute food like a father.
O Indra, having pressed the Soma, we praise you, and having won the prize of many heroic powers.
Bring us prosperity for which we long; protected by you, may we win it for ourselves and our offspring.
O hero Indra, you were born as a seer; together with Sūrya, you overcame the Dāsa tribes.
Like Soma in a flowing stream, we sustain that which was placed in secret, hidden, and concealed within the waters.
Or, being wise and desiring the favor of the seers, the inspired singer has honored the songs of the noble one.
May we be those who take delight in the *soma* juices, and likewise with the food-offerings for you, O Ratha-vīra.

These prayers, O Indra, have been recited for you; grant them to the men, O Hero, for the strength of men! Be of one mind with those in whom you take pleasure; protect both the singers and their offspring.
Hear the call, O heroic Indra; you are praised by the hymns of Venya, the son of Pr̥thi.
Your chariot has roared toward your ghee-filled womb; like a wave rushing down slopes, your swift horses have sped forth.
With his supports, Savitṛ has made the earth firm; in the pillarless space, Savitṛ has propped up the heavens.
Like a horse, Savitṛ has milked the roaring ocean from the midst of the atmosphere, which was bound within the untraversed space.

Where the ocean, firmly supported, poured forth, Savitṛ, the Son of Waters, knows that place. From there the world arose; from there the realm of dust emerged; from there heaven and earth were spread out.
Then this other, worthy of sacrifice, came into being through the abundance of the immortal world:
the fair-winged Garuḍa of Savitar was indeed born first; he is his follower.
Like cattle to the village, like a warrior to his horses, like a lowing cow with a kindly mind milking for her calf—so [did she come].
Like a husband unto his wife, may Savitṛ, the sustainer of heaven, the possessor of all boons, descend upon us.
As Hiraṇyastūpa, the Aṅgiras, invoked you, O Savitṛ, for this prize of battle, so do I,
praising and adoring you for protection, watch for you as one watches the stalk of Soma.
Though already kindled, you are kindled again, O bearer of oblations to the gods.
Come to us with the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus; come to us for our mercy.
Accepting this sacrifice and this speech, draw near to us.
O kindled one, we mortals invoke you; we invoke you for the sake of mercy.
I praise you, Jātavedas, the possessor of all boons, with my inspired thought.
O Agni, bring hither to us the gods who follow the dear law, for the sake of mercy—the gods who follow the dear law.
Agni the god became the domestic priest of the gods; men and seers have kindled Agni.
I invoke Agni, the winner of great wealth, for his favor and for the winning of wealth.
Agni protected Atri, Bharadvāja, Gaviṣṭhira, Kaṇva, Trasadasyu, and us in the contest for cattle.
Vasiṣṭha invokes Agni as his domestic priest; for the sake of mercy, he invokes him as his domestic priest.
By faith Agni is kindled; by faith the oblation is offered.
We proclaim faith upon the head of Bhaga with our speech.
O Śraddhā, make dear the gift of the one who gives, and dear the intent of the one who wishes to give; make this which has been uttered by me dear to the sacrificers at their feasts.
Just as the gods established faith among the fierce Asuras, so [make it dear].
O gods, make this [sacrifice] prosper among our patrons who offer oblations. The sacrificers, protected by Vāyu, worship faith with the heart’s intention; through faith, one finds wealth.
We invoke Faith at dawn; we invoke Faith at midday;
we invoke Faith at the setting of the sun. O Faith, inspire us with faith here!
Truly, he is a great ruler, the wondrous devourer of enemies.
He whose friend is never slain and who is never defeated at any time—
may that Indra, the bestower of well-being, the lord of the people, the slayer of Vṛtra, the subduer of enemies, the wielder of power,
the bull, the drinker of Soma, and the creator of fearlessness, go before us.
Drive away the demon, strike down the adversaries; break asunder the jaws of Vṛtra.
O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, quell the fury of the enemy who assails us.
O Indra, strike down our enemies; cast those who attack us low.
Whoever seeks to harm us, send him down into the lowest darkness. O Indra, turn away the mind of the hater; turn away the weapon of him who desires to conquer us.
Grant us protection from his wrath; drive far away his deadly blow.
Moving to and fro, the active ones wait upon Indra at his birth,
having obtained excellent heroic power.
O Indra, you were born from strength, from force, and from might.
O Bull, you are indeed a bull;
O Indra, you are the slayer of Vṛtra. You have extended across the mid-air and propped up the heavens with your might.
O Indra, you bear in your arms the *ark* that is in harmony with you; whetting the thunderbolt with your might,
O Indra, you are the conqueror of all beings by your power.
He has become the source of all existence.
For some, Soma flows clear; others worship clarified butter;
to those for whom the honey flows, may he go even unto them.
Those who are invincible through austerity, those who have gone to heaven through austerity,
and those who have performed great austerity— go even to them.
Those who fight in the forefronts of battle, the heroes who lay down their lives.
Go even to those who have given a thousand as sacrificial fees. Go even to those ancient ones who were observers of *ṛta*, followers of *ṛta*, and increasers of *ṛta*—
to those ancestors rich in ascetic fervor, O Yama, go even to them.
May [this oblation] go to the thousand-pathed seers who protect the sun,
and to the rishis who practice austerity, O Yama— to those born of austerity.
O one-eyed, misshapen, and deformed Arayi, you who always pursue [your prey], go to the mountain!
With the powers of Śirimbiṭha, with those we drive you away. Driven away from here, driven away from there—let Āruṣī destroy all the embryos.
O Brahmaṇaspati, O sharp-horned bull, strike down the Arāyī.
That wood which floats there on the far shore of the river, devoid of men—seize it, O you of evil intent; with it, go to the furthermost distance.
For when you have gone forward, O frogs, with your bellies stained like rust...
Slain are all the enemies of Indra; they have vanished like bubbles.
These men have led forth the cow; they have carried around the fire.
They have established glory among the gods—who indeed would dare to attack them?
May our prayers impel Agni, like a swift steed in races;
through him may we win prize after prize.
O Agni, with that host of yours, aided by you, may we drive back the cattle.
Impel her toward us for the winning of wealth. O Agni, bring us solid wealth—broad, rich in cattle and horses; turn the niggardly miser upside down.
O Agni, you have caused the unaging star, the sun, to ascend to heaven;
you have established light for all people.
O Agni, you are the banner of the tribes, the most beloved and the most excellent, seated upon the sacrificial altar.
Awake for the singer, bestowing vital strength!
May we now, O Indra and all the gods, bring these worlds to fulfillment.
May Indra, together with the Ādityas, fashion for us the sacrifice, our bodies, and our progeny.
May Indra, together with the Ādityas and the host of Maruts, be the protector of our bodies.
When the gods went forth after slaying the Asuras, guarding their divine status,
they brought the sun back by their powers and beheld the vigorous self-sustaining power (svadhā) all around.
May Sūrya protect us from heaven; may Vāta [protect us] from the intermediate space;
may Agni [protect us] from earthly beings.
Be pleased, O Savitṛ, whose flame is worthy of a hundred libations.
Protect us from the falling lightning bolt. May the god Savitṛ grant us sight; may Parvata also grant us sight;
may Dhātṛ bestow sight upon us.
Bestow sight upon our eye, sight for our bodies to see clearly;
may we behold this world together and discern it apart.
O Sūrya, may we gaze upon you, who are so beautiful to behold.
May we look upon those who have no sight for falsehood.
Yonder sun has risen; my good fortune has risen. Knowing this, I, the all-conquering one, have gazed upon my husband.
I am the banner, I am the head; I am the fierce one who pronounces the verdict.
May my husband attend to the will of me, the victorious woman. My sons are slayers of enemies, and my daughter is a sovereign queen.

And I am victorious; my fame is supreme among my husband. By that oblation through which Indra became glorious and most excellent— O gods, I have performed this very rite; indeed, I have become free from rivals.

Free from rivals, slayer of rivals, victorious, and overpowering, I have seized the splendor of these others, as one might take the wealth of those who are weaker. I have completely conquered these co-wives, being myself the conqueror.
RV 10.159.6: So that I may rule over this hero and over the people.
RV 10.160.1: Drink of this strong, invigorating [Soma]; unyoke both bay steeds here along with the chariot.
O Indra, let not other sacrificers detain you; these pressed juices are for you alone.

For you the juices have been pressed; for you let them be pressed. The strengthening songs call upon you, O Indra. Taking pleasure today in this libation, you who know all things, drink the Soma here. He who, with longing mind and with his whole heart, desiring the gods, presses the Soma for him—
Indra does not give away the cattle of that man; he makes for him what is praiseworthy and lovely.
He is clearly seen by this man who, though wealthy, does not press Soma for him. The bountiful Lord casts him down into the pit; he slays the haters of prayer without being commanded.
Desiring horses, desiring cattle, desiring strength, we invoke you that you may come to us. Abiding in your new favor, O Indra, may we call upon you for our well-being.
I release you by means of this oblation so that you may live—freed from unknown consumption and from the upper consumption.
If the Grāhi has seized him, whether she has indeed taken hold of him, may Indra and Agni release him from her.

Whether his life-span is exhausted, or whether he has departed, or if he has been led even to the very presence of Death— I bring him back from the lap of Nirṛti; I have rescued him for a hundred autumns.
With an oblation that has a thousand eyes, a hundred autumns, and a hundred lives, I have rescued him. So that Indra may lead him for a hundred autumns to the further shore of all misfortune.
Live for a hundred autumns, prospering; live for a hundred winters and a hundred springs.

May Indra, Agni, Savitṛ, and Bṛhaspati restore this man to life through this hundredfold oblation. I have brought you back; I have found you. You have returned, renewed. With all your limbs whole, I have found for you full sight and a full span of life.

May Agni, in harmony with the sacred word (*brahman*), the slayer of demons, drive away from here the disease that has settled upon your embryo or has taken up its abode in your womb, bearing an evil name. May that which has settled upon your embryo or has taken up its abode in your womb, bearing an evil name, be driven away.
Agni, together with the sacred word (*brahman*), has driven away the flesh-eater.
That which kills your flying [offspring], that which kills your one who is about to sit down,
or your one who crawls— that which seeks to destroy what has been born, we cause it to perish from here.
He who spreads apart your thighs and lies between the husband and wife, he who licks the womb from within— him we cause to perish utterly.
He who, having become your brother, your husband, or your lover, lies with you...
We cause him to perish from here, whoever seeks to destroy your offspring.
He who, having deluded you with sleep and darkness,
lies in wait— we cause him to perish from here, whoever seeks to destroy your offspring.
From your eyes, from your nostrils, from your ears, and from your chin—
I root out the consumption (*yakṣma*) from your head, from your brain, and from your tongue.
From your necks, from your *uṣṇihā* joints, from your vertebrae, and from your spine—
I tear away from you the consumption in the forearms, from the shoulders, and from the upper arms.
From your intestines, from your bowels, from the rectum, and from the heart;
from the kidneys, from the liver, and from the lungs, I tear away your consumption.
From your two thighs, from your two knee-caps, from your two heels, and from your two foreparts;
from your two hips and from your buttocks, I pull the disease away from you.
From your urethra, from your penis, from your body hairs, and from your nails.

That consumption which has arisen from every part of your body, that I now tear away from you. From limb by limb, from hair by hair, from joint by joint— that consumption which has arisen from every part of your body, that I now tear away from you.
Depart, O Lord of the mind; go away and move far off.
Proclaim to Nirṛti that the mind of the living man wanders in many directions.
Indeed, they choose a blessed boon; they yoke the right hand for what is auspicious.
May there be auspiciousness; may the eye be with Vaivasvata, and may the mind of the living man be directed in many ways.
Whatever we have committed through longing, through reviling, or through imprecation, whether waking or sleeping—may Agni place all those unwelcome misdeeds far away from us.
O Indra, O Brahmanaspati, whatever offense we have committed against you, may the wise Aṅgiras protect us from the enmity and distress of our haters.
Today we have conquered; we have attained our goal; we have become free from sin.

RV 10.164.5: May that evil intention which arises while waking or sleeping reach him whom we hate; may it reach him who hates us. RV 10.165.1–2: O Gods, whatever the dove has come here seeking, sent as a messenger by Nirṛti, for that let us offer worship and perform atonement; may there be well-being for our bipeds and our quadrupeds.
May the dove sent to us be auspicious; O gods, may the bird be harmless in our homes.
May Agni, the sage, accept our oblation; may the winged missile spare us.
Let not the winged missile harm us; it makes its footprint upon the hearth in the place of the fire.
May there be peace for our cattle and for our men; O gods, let not the dove harm us here.
Whatever the owl cries out is in vain, as is whatever footprint the dove makes upon the fire.
He to whom this one has been sent as a messenger—to that Yama, to Death, let there be homage.
Drive away the dove with a *ṛc*; we drive it out. Rejoicing in the sacrificial food (*iṣ*), lead the cow around us.
Driving away all misfortunes, let it fly away, leaving us strength; let it fly most swiftly. Make me a bull among my equals, a subduer of my rivals.
Make me the slayer of my enemies, the sovereign lord of cattle. I am here, like Indra, unharmed and uninjured, having cast my rivals beneath my feet; all these others stand under my dominion.

Right here I bind you fast, as if two bow-ends with a string. O Lord of Speech, restrain these [words] so that they may speak only what is favorable to me. I have come as a conqueror, by means of the power of Viśvakarman.
I have won over your mind, I have won over your vow, I have won over your assembly.
Having taken possession of your security and well-being, may I be preeminent among you. I have stepped upon your heads;
let those who are beneath my feet cry out like frogs from the water—like frogs from the water.
For you, O Indra, this honey is poured out; you are the sovereign of the pressed vessel.
Bestow upon us wealth consisting of many heroes; you, having undergone fervent heat, have won the light of heaven.
We invoke Śakra, the conqueror of heaven, who rejoices greatly in the soma-juice, for the sake of the pressed draughts.
Take note of this sacrifice of ours here; come hither! We pray for Maghavan, who conquers the rivals.
Under the law of King Soma and Varuṇa, and within the protection of Bṛhaspati and Anumati— O Maghavan, O Ordainer, O Disposer, today at this hymn of praise, I have partaken of the jars.
Impelled, I have made this food my portion; as the first sage, I have polished this hymn of praise.
When the soma was pressed, O Viśvāmitra and Jamadagni, I came to you both in your dwelling with a gift.
Now, indeed, the greatness of Vāta’s chariot comes forth; rending [the air], his roar goes thundering.
Touching the sky, he goes forth making the regions red; then he comes, scattering the dust of the earth.
The various manifestations of the wind rush after him; like women to a festival, they come to meet him.
With them, the god travels on a single chariot; he is the king of this entire world.

Traveling by paths through the intermediate space, he does not rest for even a single day. The friend of the waters, the first-born, the upholder of *ṛta*—where indeed was he born, and from whence did he come into being?
The self of the gods, the germ of the world, this god moves according to his own will.
His roars alone are heard, not his form; to him, that wind, let us pay worship with an oblation.
May the wind blow pleasantly upon our cows; may they graze upon herbs rich in nourishment.
May they drink from waters full of fatness, which bring wealth to living beings; O Rudra, have mercy on those who walk upon their feet.
Those who are alike, those who are diverse, and those who are of one form—those whose names Agni knows through sacrifice;
those whom the Aṅgirases created here for the sake of heat—to them, O Parjanya, grant great protection.
Those who offered their bodies among the gods, whose every form Soma knows.
May they, swelling with milk, rich in offspring, be granted to us in Indra’s cow-pen. Prajāpati, bestowing these upon me, in harmony with all the gods and the ancestors,
having brought them as auspicious ones into our cow-pen, may we abide together with their progeny.
May the radiant, lofty one drink the Soma-mead, bestowing unimpaired life upon the lord of the sacrifice.
He who, impelled by the wind, protects by his own self, has nourished all creatures and shines forth in many ways.
The radiant, lofty, well-sustained, most victorious one—truth established upon the foundation of heaven according to the cosmic law.
