The slayer of enemies, the slayer of Vṛtra, the greatest slayer of Dasyus, the slayer of Asuras, the slayer of rivals—light has been born.
This is the best, the highest light among lights; it is called all-conquering, wealth-winning, and vast.
All-illuminating, with great radiance, Sūrya has spread wide for us to see, together with unfailing power.
Radiant with light, he has gone to the sun, to the luminous realm of heaven,
by whom all these worlds were brought together— by Viśvakarman, who is favored by all the gods. O Indra, you protected that chariot of the one who presses the Soma and offers oblations.
You heard the call of the Soma-presser;
you struck off the head of the turbulent Makha from his skin and went to the house of the Soma-presser.
O Indra, you [unbound] that mortal Venya for Āstrabudhna, who was longing for him, again and again, for the sake of the one who meditates upon you. O Indra, place that Sūrya, who is behind, in front.
Even beyond the will of the gods, come hither with thy wood; the cows follow thy path with their full udders.
Come hither with thy wealth-bestowing thought, thou most liberal one, awakening the sacrifice with thy bounteous gifts.
Like those who weave a thread, we, the bounteous givers, have taken up the thread; we sacrifice.
Dawn drives away the darkness of her sister and turns the path back by virtue of her noble birth.
I have brought you here; abide within me, stand firm and unshakable.
May all the subjects desire you; let not the kingdom fall away from you.
Be right here, do not waver; be as immovable as a mountain. Stand firm here like Indra; maintain the kingdom right here.
Indra has established this [world] as firm with a firm oblation;
may Soma speak in its favor, and may Brahmaṇaspati likewise. Firm is the sky, firm is the earth, and firm are these mountains.
Firm is this entire world; firm is this king of the people.
Firm for you let King Varuṇa, firm let the god Bṛhaspati, and firm let both Indra and Agni maintain your kingdom.
With the firm oblation, we touch Soma with that which is firm; and so may Indra make the clans bring tribute exclusively to us.
With the oblation called *abhīvarta*, by which Indra was turned toward victory—
With that, O Brahmaṇaspati, turn us toward sovereignty.
Having turned [against them], overcome our rivals and those who are hostile to us; overcome those who attack us and him who bears malice toward us.

May the god Savitṛ turn you toward [us], may Soma turn you toward us; may all beings turn toward you, so that you shall be the one who overcomes. By means of that oblation by which Indra became preeminent in glory after performing his deed—
O gods, I have performed this rite; indeed, I have become free from rivals.
Free from rivals, a slayer of rivals, a sovereign ruler, and all-conquering— may I be the supreme lord over these beings and over the people.
O pressing-stones, may the god Savitṛ impel you forward according to the sacred law. Be yoked to the pole; press out the juice! O stones, drive away misfortune and drive away ill-will.
O Dawns, prepare the healing medicine! The pressing-stones,
in unison, exult upon the lower stones,
bestowing manly vigor upon the Bull.
O pressing-stones, may the god Savitṛ now impel you according to the sacred law for the sake of the sacrificer who pours the libation.
The sons of the Ṛbhus have loudly shouted their great songs of praise from the sacrificial enclosure.
Those who dwell upon the earth, the sustainers of all, devour [the offerings] as a calf devours its mother-cow.
Bring forth the god Jātavedas with divine prayer;
may he carry our oblations to him in due succession.

This one here, seeking the gods, is led forth as the Hotṛ priest for the sacrifice. Their chariot, covered all around, like the sun, shines by its own nature. This Agni protects us, as if from birth itself, as from the immortal.
The god, more powerful than even power itself, has been fashioned for the sake of life.

The wise, with their heart and mind, behold the winged one anointed by the magic power (*māyā*) of the Asura. Within the ocean, the seers (*kavayaḥ*) look out; the ordainers (*vedhasaḥ*) seek his station among the rays of light.
The winged one bears speech with his mind; the Gandharva spoke it within the womb. At the station of Cosmic Order (Ṛta), the birds protect that shining, celestial wisdom.
I beheld the herdsman, who never rests, moving hither and thither along his paths.
He, clothing himself in converging and diverging rays, revolves repeatedly within the worlds.

That very steed, impelled by the gods, victorious, the overcomer of chariots— him, the swift one with uninjured fellies, the conqueror in battle, the descendant of Ṛkṣa, we invoke here for our well-being.
Invoking the bounty of Indra as it were, may we ascend [you] for our well-being, as if onto a ship.
O you two who are wide, broad, vast, and deep, may we not suffer harm through these [near] waters, nor through those beyond.
He who, by his might, in an instant has overspread the five peoples with light, like the sun with its radiance.
Winning thousands, winning hundreds, his speed cannot be checked, like a young woman or an arrow.
Arise, look upon Indra’s seasonal portion! If it is cooked, offer it; if it is not yet cooked, wait until it is ready.
The oblation is cooked; O Indra, come hither! The sun has reached the midpoint of his journey.
Your friends sit around you with their treasures, like guardians of the clan surrounding the lord of the migration as he wanders.
I consider it cooked in the udder, cooked on the fire; I consider that newest truth well-cooked.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, performer of many deeds, drink with pleasure the curd of the midday libation.

O much-invoked one, you have utterly subdued your enemies; let your strength be supreme, and let your bounty be here. O Indra, bring us riches with your right hand; you are the lord of the wealthy rivers.
Like a fearsome beast, roaming and dwelling in the mountains, you have come hither from the farthest distance.
O Indra, whetting your sharp bolt and your keen blade, strike down our enemies and drive away those who oppose us.
O Indra, you were born for dominion, for excellent strength, as the bull of the peoples.
You drove away the unfriendly folk and made wide space for the gods.
Of him whose [sacrifice] was *pratha* and *sapratha*, of the *anuṣṭubh* oblation, of the oblation itself—
From Dhātṛ, from Dyutāna Savitṛ, and from Viṣṇu, Vasiṣṭha brought forth the *rathantara*.
They found that which was placed beyond reach, the supreme abode of sacrifice hidden in the cave.

From Dhātṛ, from the radiant Savitṛ, and from Viṣṇu, Bharadvāja brought forth the great [hymn] of Agni. They, meditating with their minds, found the first Yajus, the path traveled by the gods, which had been scattered.
From Dhātṛ, Dyutāna, Savitṛ, and Viṣṇu, these have brought forth the Gharma from the Sun.

May Bṛhaspati lead us across difficult passages; may he drive away the evil-minded one who intends harm. May he cast off the curse and strike down ill-will, and then provide the sacrificer with well-being and prosperity.
May Narāśaṃsa protect us at the *prayāja* offering; may the *anuyāja* be auspicious for us in our invocations.
May he swiftly strike away the curse and the evil thought, and then provide the sacrificer with prosperity and well-being.
May he whose head is heat burn up the demons who hate the sacred word (*brahman*), and may he slay them with his arrow.
Swiftly strike away the curse and the evil thought; then grant well-being and peace to the sacrificer.

I beheld you with my mind, you who are observant, born of austerity and manifested through austerity. Bestowing upon me offspring here and wealth here, beget yourself through progeny, O you who desire sons!

I beheld you with my mind as you were meditating, breathing according to the cosmic order within your own body. O young woman, rise up toward me; beget offspring through progeny, O you who desire a son!
I have placed the germ within the plants; I am within all existing beings. I have generated offspring upon the earth; I [have generated] sons from women yet to be born.
May Viṣṇu prepare the womb; may Tvaṣṭṛ fashion the forms. May Prajāpati pour [the seed]; may Dhātṛ place the embryo within you.
O Sinīvālī, bestow an embryo; O Sarasvatī, bestow an embryo.
May the two divine Aśvins, wreathed with lotuses, bestow a fetus upon you. That embryo which the Aśvins churn forth from the golden fire-sticks—
that embryo we invoke for you, so that it may be brought forth in the tenth month.
Great shall be the protection of the three— of Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa— glorious in heaven and invincible. For not even at home, nor on difficult paths, is there any [safety] apart from them.
The wicked enemy has power over him for whom the sons of Aditi bestow eternal light that he may live.
May Vāta blow toward us healing that is auspicious and delightful to our heart;
may he prolong our lives.
And you, O Vāta, are our father, and you are our brother and our friend.
Make us live for a full span of life.
O Vāta, that storehouse of immortality which is placed there in your house— grant us a portion of it so that we may live.
Send forth your voice to Agni, the bull of the peoples;
may he carry us across our enemies.
He who shines forth from the farthest distance, across the desert wastes.
May he carry us across our enemies—
he who, as a bull with his bright flame, consumes the Rākṣasas;
may he carry us across our enemies.
He who looks out upon all beings and beholds them together— may he carry us across our enemies. He,
the bright Agni, who was born on the further shore of this realm.
May he carry us across our enemies.
Now, indeed, urge forth Jātavedas, the vigorous steed,
so that he may sit upon this sacred grass of ours.
To this Jātavedas, the hero among sages, the bountiful one,
I offer a great hymn of praise.
Those rays of Jātavedas which carry the oblation to the gods— [to him I offer it].
May he further our sacrifice with them.
This spotted bull has stepped forth; he has settled before his mother, and as he goes toward heaven, he approaches his father.
Moving within the luminous realms, he breathes out from his breath;
the Great One has illumined the sky.
He rules over thirty domains; speech is bestowed upon the bird.
Day by day, at every moment; from the kindling of fervent heat (*tapas*), *Ṛta* and *Satya* were born. From that, night was born; from that, the billowing ocean arose.
From the ocean, the billowing sea, the year was born;
ordaining days and nights, he who holds sway over all that blinks his eyes.
Dhātṛ fashioned the sun and the moon according to their ancient order.
Heaven and earth, the mid-air, and likewise the light of heaven—O bull-like Agni, noble one, you gather all these together with your fuel.
You are kindled at the place of *iḷā*; bring us wealth.

Come together, speak together; let your minds be in accord, so that as the ancient gods, being in agreement, attend to their portion. Common be the counsel, common the assembly, common the mind, and united the thought of these.
I address you with a common prayer; I offer to you with a common oblation. Common be your resolve, common your hearts; let your mind be one, so that you may act together in harmony.
